Date: 2026-11-22 ~23:09 IST (updated 2026-11-22 ~23:30 IST). Source: Rohan's messages.
**WHO DOES THE CODING (Rohan, 2026-11-22 ~23:30 IST): Pi on Altare writes the code, FULLY, for ALL tasks. Muse coordinates, verifies live, and deploys. (This overrides the earlier "Pi stopped for coding" instruction.)** Pi reads this file from the deploy repo and works through it; Muse pulls Pi's code back, verifies it live, and deploys it.
Standing rules that govern ALL of this: English only, no China endpoints, InstaBox Free only, cloud LLM only with Rohan's own keys. Verify live before claiming done. Fix → check in a real browser → if not fixed, fix again, without stopping. Keep ALL features and ALL options — nothing removed, hidden, merged, or renamed. The console look stays the same. Status marks: [ ] not started · [~] in progress · [x] done + live-verified · [!] blocked (reason noted).

## PART 1 — Telegram bot token entry option (Rohan: "i cant see an telgram bot tken enter option")

**Root cause (verified 2026-11-22):** There is NO Telegram token field in the web Settings UI. The token exists only as a backend config: `bot_token` in `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/conflict.py` ("telegram": ("bot_token",)), a CLI prompt in `src/qwenpaw/cli/channels_cmd.py` (`configure_telegram`, "Telegram Bot Token"), and the env var `TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_ENABLED` in `src/qwenpaw/config/channel_env.py`. A grep of the whole console source for `telegram` returns zero UI matches. The T131 spec said "setup is ONLY the bot token in Settings" — the bot was built, but the Settings field was never added. That is why Rohan cannot see it. This is MY end, not his.

- [ ] T1.1 — Find where the console Settings Channels section lives (and whether a Channels page exists at all in the web UI). If there is no Channels page, the Telegram section goes in Settings, in the same style as the other settings sections.
- [ ] T1.2 — Add a Telegram section to the web Settings UI: a "Telegram Bot Token" field (password-masked input), an Enable/Disable toggle, and a Save action. Same look as the other settings fields — no redesign, no renamed labels elsewhere.
- [ ] T1.3 — Wire the field to the real config: saving writes `bot_token` to the Telegram channel config (the same config `channels_cmd.py` writes), and the toggle writes the enabled flag. The token must be stored encrypted like the other secrets, never in plain text in the repo or in memory.
- [ ] T1.4 — Verify live in a real browser: open Settings, confirm the Telegram token field is visible, enter a test value, save, reload, confirm it persisted (masked). Then clear the test value.
- [ ] T1.5 — Verify the bot picks the token up: with a real token (Rohan enters it), confirm the Telegram bot starts, answers a DM, and the owner-approval flow works. (Needs Rohan's token — he enters it in the new field; I do NOT ask him for the token value.)
- [ ] T1.6 — Push the change to the deploy repo (Chalupandey07/qwenpaw-deploy) and rebuild/redeploy so the field is live on both Pages.

---

## PART 2 — TinyFish via Monid, ONLY the 2 free endpoints (Rohan: "monid tinyfish … this is what i wanted … that is why i added monid … see screenshot only these 2 use")

**What Rohan wants (now clear):** TinyFish THROUGH Monid, not a direct TinyFish key. He added a Monid key for this. # IMPROVEMENTS.md — every way this system can be better

Organised by area. Each item says **what**, **why it matters here**, and
**how** (concrete, with the file it touches). Ranked by value ÷ effort inside
each section. Items marked ⚑ are the ones I would do next.

Nothing here is a wish-list of generic "add AI"; every item traces to a
constraint of this deployment: one paused VM, free quotas, one user, a real
desktop that must be shared with an agent.

---

## 1. Desktop & computer-use

The desktop is the product. Current state: works, browser-verified, but the
agent burns turns on visual decisions and every failure costs a wake cycle.

| # | Improvement | Why | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 ⚑ | **Action batching with `codemode`-style scripts** | A 10-step flow is 10 model turns today; each turn needs a fresh screenshot | `features/desktop/` — add a small JS/Python "script runner" tool to the DriverCard that executes a *list* of `{click, type, wait, assert}` steps with one screenshot at the end. Only for flows with no visual branching. |
| 1.2 ⚑ | **Screenshot diffing to skip no-op turns** | The agent re-reads an unchanged screen every step | Before returning a screenshot, compare a perceptual hash against the last one; if identical, return "screen unchanged since your last action" (a few tokens) instead of a 700 KB image. Kills a large share of input tokens. |
| 1.3 | **Accessibility-tree mode first, pixels second** | Most actions (click a button, fill a field) are cheaper and more robust via the a11y tree than via coordinates | The computer-use MCP likely exposes an app/window list; extend it to return the focused app's a11y tree as text. Fall back to a screenshot only when the tree is empty. This is the single biggest reliability win for form-filling. |
| 1.4 | **Deterministic replay of taught skills** | Teach-by-showing records events but replays are re-reasoned | Store the recorded event list with the skill; on replay, execute events directly and only ask the model when a selector fails. Turns a 15-step taught task into ~1 turn. |
| 1.5 | **Per-computer resource budgets** | Two Xvfb displays + two Chromiums on 8 GB | Track RSS per display; refuse a third private computer before the box swaps. Report free RAM in `__status`. |
| 1.6 | **Screen-generation garbage collection** | Generations only grow; old capabilities linger in KV until TTL | On release, optionally delete capabilities older than one generation. Cheap hygiene once on D1. |
| 1.7 | **Terminal session expiry tied to the lease** | See BUGS.md B-4 — fixed for *minting*; an already-open socket still lives | On lease release, the Worker cannot close a live WS; instead have `pty-server.py` poll the control file every 5 s and `SIGHUP` the shell when the lease ends. |
| 1.8 | **Wake-cost awareness** | Every probe can wake the box and burn run minutes | The chrome already avoids waking on preview click. Extend: batch `/desktop/__status` polls to one per tab, and show "last wake cost" in the status page. |

## 2. Memory & self-learning

Current: bounded recall CLI, lessons ledger, ReMe doctor, and **consolidation**
(T83) which turns daily logs into lesson candidates. Upstream FTS5 does the
search. Ripwire is installed and documented (T73).

| # | Improvement | Why | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 ⚑ | **Apply the lessons ledger to the live MEMORY.md** | The tooling exists (including `consolidate.py` for the cron path); the agent does not use it yet | Add a step to the system prompt (`features/infra/prompts/v1/AGENTS.md`): at a checkpoint, `lessons.py propose` at most 1–3 candidates, and never `accept` without the user. |
| 2.2 ⚑ | **Fix ReMe's actual cause** | `memory/` is empty; the doctor names five causes but nobody has run it live | One command on the box (`reme_doctor.py`) → it prints the cause. # AGENT-DESIGN.md — the best agent this system can be

This is the design answer to "make it the best agent", written against *this*
repo's real constraints: one paused VM, free quotas, one human, a real desktop
shared with an agent, cloud LLM only.

It is deliberately not a generic "agent architecture" essay. Every decision
below is one this deployment can actually implement, and most say which file
it lands in.

---

## 1. What makes an agent good here

Not "more autonomy". The failure modes in this repo's incident log are almost
all *the agent believing something that was not true*:

- reported an admin login worked when it did not;
- trusted `installed: true` while the binary was gone;
- trusted a minted token without decoding its payload;
- reported completion without a live check.

So the design principle is:

> **The agent's scarce resource is not tokens or turns. It is *trustworthy
> belief*.** Every mechanism below exists to make a true belief cheap and a
> false one expensive.

That gives five design pillars.

## 2. Pillar 1 — Ground truth before claims

**The rule:** a claim about system state must be produced by a check that can
fail, and the check must be named.

**In practice:**

| Claim | Must be produced by | Never by |
|---|---|---|
| "the desktop is live" | `__status` → `desktop:"up"` **and** the RFB probe | a screenshot alone |
| "Chromium is installed" | the binary exists (`test -x /usr/lib/chromium/chromium`) | a stale `installed: true` marker |
| "the deploy succeeded" | the provider's status **and** a live fetch | the deploy command's exit code |
| "the screen link works" | a WS upgrade returning 101 | a mint returning 200 |
| "memory is fixed" | `reme_doctor` reporting a cause is gone | notes appearing once |

**Implemented:** `verifyCapability` re-checks on connect; `preflight.py`
gates a browser round; the harnesses fail on the old code by construction
(each fix has a test that the *previous* commit fails).

**Next:** `--verify` claims from ripwire for code questions
(`features/memory/skills/ripwire/`), and the `report-completion-only-when-
confirmed` lesson already in the ledger design.

## 3. Pillar 2 — Cheap senses, expensive judgment

The desktop loop is observe → decide → act, and observation is the expensive
part (a 243–707 KB screenshot per step). Three changes make sensing cheap
without losing judgment:

1. **Screenshot diffing** (IMPROVEMENTS §1.2). Return "screen unchanged since
   your last action" — a few tokens — instead of an identical PNG. The model
   loses nothing: an unchanged screen is not new information.
2. **Accessibility tree before pixels** (§1.3). "Click the *Save* button" is
   cheaper and more robust via the a11y tree than via coordinates. Use pixels
   only when the tree is empty (canvas, game, image-only UI).
3. **One screenshot per batch** (§1.1). For flows with no visual branching,
   execute a list of steps and observe once at the end.

Together these attack the single biggest cost in the system, and they make
the agent *more* accurate — coordinates break when a layout shifts; a named
control does not.

## 4. Pillar 3 — Memory that is bounded and honest

**Implemented now:** `recall.py` (2,000-token hard cap, 3 results, credential
redaction, out-of-loop), `lessons.py` (candidate/accept ledger, ≤10 accepted,
secrets rejected), `reme_doctor.py` (names the five real gates).

**The design that completes it:**

- **Read whole at start, search never.** MEMORY.md is read in full at task
  start (it is small and curated); `recall.py` is for looking *backwards*
  into history, not for knowing who you are.
- **Lessons are earned, not generated.** A lesson must come from a failure
  that actually happened, carry the date and session, and state a *future
  action*. The ledger refuses entries without Evidence and rejects anything
  credential-shaped rather than scrubbing it — a lesson containing a token is
  a bug upstream.
- **The reflection step is capped.** ≤3 candidates pending

# AGENTS.md — working on the QwenPaw deployment

You are working on **`Chalupandey07/qwenpaw-deploy`**: the control plane for a
QwenPaw agent running on an InstaBox **Free** machine, fronted by Cloudflare
Pages + Workers. This file is the contract. Read it before touching anything.

Keep this file under **20,000 characters** — the size an agent loads whole.
Put long rules in the owning feature guide and leave a one-line pointer
here. **Every new rule cites an incident:** the date + the failure that paid
for it (see `docs/LESSONS.md` for the full symptom → cause → fix story).
A convention that lives only in prose gets violated within a week; a rule +
a mechanical check survives — the checks live in `scripts/checks/` and run
before every push (see §5).

---

## 1. The one rule

**Nothing is "done" until it is verified live by whoever can see the live
system.** Code that compiles, a harness that passes, and a protocol check are
*evidence*, never *proof*. Write down which of the three you have.

The two known failure modes this rule exists to stop:

- A deploy-generated admin password was reported as working ("login 200") for
  hours; the real account was a different user. **Verify the actual thing.**
  (2026-11-15, docs/LESSONS.md.)
- A browser round lost three tests to a spent Cloudflare KV write quota that
  no protocol test could see. **Check the quota before spending a session.**
  (2026-11-15/17, docs/LESSONS.md.)
- A rendered `docker run --tmpfs` with a bare size (`16m` instead of
  `size=16m`) passed 50/50 machine-free and failed live with exit 125.
  **Validate rendered commands against the tool's real option grammar, and
  run the rendering live the first time it executes.** (2026-11-19,
  docs/LESSONS.md.)
- A control that silently reverts looks broken — show the server's reason
  next to it. A load-bearing guard scoped to a whole ancestor hides
  legitimate renames — scope it to code-like parents only. (2026-11-19,
  docs/LESSONS.md.)
- A hide/match rule must use the control's real live label, not a label
  found in the bundle's strings for another screen — verify against the
  live DOM. A display name may render truncated — rename the truncated
  form too, never only the full phrase. (2026-11-19, docs/LESSONS.md.)
- Before assuming a live UI element belongs to the upstream app, grep the
  deployed bundles for its distinguishing string; if the string exists
  nowhere in the app, the element is ours. (2026-11-19, docs/LESSONS.md.)
- An injected element that can be created under different anchors needs a
  document-wide guard, never an anchor-scoped one — the anchor can resolve
  to a different container on different passes. (2026-11-19,
  docs/LESSONS.md.)
- Never patch a content-hashed asset in place when it is served immutable
  — the browser keeps the old bytes under the same name; change the URL
  (rename the file or add a version query) or the fix never reaches the
  tab. (2026-11-19, docs/LESSONS.md.)
- A timestamp that is only written on change is a stale clock, not an
  uptime source — guard uptime needs its own run-start observation, set
  at the down→up transition and never refreshed while up; and a fix that
  only fires on a future state transition is dead code when the live
  state is already past it — reconcile the current state on the next
  tick. (2026-11-19, docs/LESSONS.md.)

**When you learn something new:** add the one-line rule here and the full
symptom → cause → fix story to `docs/LESSONS.md` (append-only, timestamped,
never rewritten). If the lesson can be checked mechanically, add a check
under `scripts/checks/` — the check is the backup.

## 2. Division of labour

| Role | Who | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Code + docs | the coding agent (AutoClaw) | edits the repo, runs local harnesses, commits to `main` |
| Deploy + live verify | Muse | deploys Workers/Pages, syncs machine files, drives a real browser, records results |

If you are the coding agent: **never claim anything is live.** Commit, state

- A hide/match rule must use the control's real live label, not a label
  found in the bundle's strings for another screen — verify against the
  live DOM. A display name may render truncated — rename the truncated
  form too, never only the full phrase. (2026-11-19, docs/LESSONS.md.)

  deployed bundles for its distinguishing string; if the string exists
  nowhere in the app, the element is ours. (2026-11-19, docs/LESSONS.md.)

  document-wide guard, never an anchor-scoped one — the anchor can resolve
  to a different container on different passes. (2026-11-19,
  docs/LESSONS.md.)

# Camoufox × QwenPaw integration-seam research — 2026-11-15

Research only. Nothing installed, edited, restarted, or snapshotted.
Machine `m_agq5wqqo2fvypym7rjlpvngc2m` (InstaBox Free, Debian 13), QwenPaw
`agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`, container `qwenpaw` (Up, healthy).
GPT Astra was tried once for a design sanity-check and timed out after 120 s
(no answer); every conclusion below is from source read live on the machine,
not from Astra.

## TL;DR verdict

**No — QwenPaw's SDK cannot be pointed at Camoufox directly.** There is no
config knob, env var, or endpoint that does it. All three "obvious" seams
are dead ends (evidence in §1). A bridge is required. The smallest honest
designs are §2; recommended is **Option C** (Playwright-server + a small
QwenPaw `ControlLink` patch) if patching QwenPaw is acceptable, else
**Option B** (standalone HTTP bridge + a QwenPaw skill) if QwenPaw must stay
pristine. Camoufox itself must run in **its own venv on the host**
(or a sidecar container), never inside QwenPaw's venv/image.

---

## 1. The exact seams (with file:line quotes)

### 1a. QwenPaw only speaks Chromium — by construction

Config — `/app/src/qwenpaw/config/config.py:3294-3362` (`BrowserConfig`):

```python
class BrowserConfig(BaseModel):
    backend: Literal["auto", "launch", "managed_cdp", "connect_cdp"] = "auto"
    ...
    cdp_url: Optional[str] = None
    cdp_port: int = 0
    engine: Literal["auto", "chromium"] = "auto"   # <-- firefox is NOT a value
    channel: Optional[str] = None
    executable_path: Optional[str] = None
```

```python
# config.py, _migrate_unsupported_engine (field_validator on "engine")
if value in {"webkit", "firefox"}:
    logger.warning(
        "browser.engine %r is not supported by the unified browser; "
        "falling back to auto", value,
    )
    return "auto"
```

So `browser.engine="firefox"` is silently rewritten to `"auto"` (= Chromium).
Live config confirms the defaults (`/app/working/config.json`, i.e.
`/data/home/qwenpaw/working/config.json` on the host):

```json
{"backend": "auto", "engine": "auto", "executable_path": null,
 "cdp_url": null, "cdp_port": 0, "channel": null, "headless": "auto", ...}
```

Identity routing — `/app/src/qwenpaw/browser/runtime/identity.py:7-10`:

```python
_ENGINE_VARIANT = {
    "auto": "playwright",
    "launch": "playwright",
    "managed_cdp": "cdp",
    "connect_cdp": "cdp",
}
```

Only two variants exist: `playwright` and `cdp` (plus `chrome` for the
extension identity). There is no firefox variant to select.

### 1b. The Playwright path hard-codes `chromium.launch`

`/app/src/qwenpaw/browser/control_link/playwright/adapter.py:71-95`
(`_build_launch_kwargs`):

```python
engine = str(params.get("engine") or "chromium")
if engine != "chromium":
    raise _fatal(f"engine not wired yet: {engine}", engine)
launch: dict[str, Any] = {"headless": bool(params.get("headless", True))}
channel, executable_path = _resolved_launch_binary(params)
if channel:
    launch["channel"] = channel
elif executable_path:
    launch["executable_path"] = executable_path
```

`/app/src/qwenpaw/browser/control_link/playwright/adapter.py:381,397`
(`_create_session_context` — the only two launch calls in the file):

```python
context = await self._pw.chromium.launch_persistent_context(
    user_data_dir, **launch_kwargs, **context_kwargs)
...
browser = await self._pw.chromium.launch(**launch_kwargs)
```

A repo-wide grep over `/app/src/qwenpaw/browser/*.py` finds **zero**
occurrences of `firefox`, zero of `connect_over_cdp`, zero of any
`playwright.*.connect(` call. The string `firefox` appears only as
`firefox_user_prefs` in Camoufox's own docs, never in QwenPaw code.

**Dead end 1 — `executable_path` → Camoufox binary:** the path is passed to
`chromium.launch()`. Playwright would exec a Firefox binary with Chromium
flags/expectations and fail. It is a Chromium-binary knob, not a
bring-your-own-engine knob.

**Dead end 2 — `connect_cdp` → Camoufox:** the CDP backend is Chromium C

# QwenPaw on InstaBox Free

An AI agent with a **real desktop it can drive**, running on a free-tier VM,
fronted by Cloudflare. You can watch it work, take control, and hand control
back — from the console, in a browser.

**Constraints that shape everything:** InstaBox Free only · Cloudflare free
tier only · English only · no China endpoints · cloud LLM only with your own
keys · no local models.

---

## Start here

| If you want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| Understand the whole system in 10 minutes | **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** |
| Know what is done, in progress, and blocked | **[PLAN.md](PLAN.md)** · [STATUS.md](STATUS.md) |
| Contribute code (rules, tests, quota discipline) | **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** |
| See every known bug, with severity and fix | **[BUGS.md](BUGS.md)** |
| Find the next thing worth building | **[IMPROVEMENTS.md](IMPROVEMENTS.md)** |
| Understand the agent design philosophy | **[AGENT-DESIGN.md](AGENT-DESIGN.md)** |
| Know what Muse hit and fixed, in detail | [HANDOFF-AUTOCLAW.md](HANDOFF-AUTOCLAW.md) · `features/desktop/README.md` (removed 2026-11-15 → features/computer/README.md) |

## Live

- **Console (use this):** https://qwenpawx.pages.dev — root `/` **is** the
  QwenPaw console, served through the Pages proxy. Backup:
  https://qwenpaw-frontend.pages.dev
- **Desktop:** https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/desktop
- **Status / wake page:** https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/status
- **Origin (direct, works but no proxy):**
  https://8088-agq5wqqo2fvypym7rjlpvngc2m.instabox.tech

**Login:** QwenPaw allows exactly one account. The account on the machine is
`satwik`, created by web registration — **not** from `.env`, so the `.env`
password does not work. Log in with the password chosen at registration.

If that password is lost: delete `working.secret/auth.json` on the machine and
restart the container; QwenPaw recreates the admin from
`QWENPAW_AUTH_USERNAME` / `QWENPAW_AUTH_PASSWORD`. **This wipes the `satwik`
account** — do it deliberately.

> `qwenpaw.pages.dev` is taken by an unrelated site and cannot be claimed. An
> empty Pages project named `qwenpaw` exists (`qwenpaw-b71.pages.dev`).

## What Free can and cannot do

| | Free tier | Consequence for this design |
|---|---|---|
| Idle pause | 30 min | a 5-min Worker cron keeps it awake; a Public-port request wakes it |
| Max run | 120 min → 480 with use | cooldown 5–135 min after a max-run pause; wakes return `409 machine_cooldown` |
| Cooldown after max run | 5–20, then 60–75, then 120–135 min | routines must tolerate a refused wake |
| Cloudflare Tunnel | **not viable** | the Pages proxy is the front door instead |
| Snapshots | max 5, create can 429 | keep one verified restore point |

Cloudflare free limits that actually bite: **KV 1,000 writes/day** (already
burned once), D1 100,000 rows written/day + 5,000,000 rows read/day,
Workers 100,000 requests/day, Durable Objects 100,000 requests/day.
See `AGENTS.md` §6 for the per-service budget rules this repo follows.

## Repo layout

```
AGENTS.md          the working contract (read before coding)
ARCHITECTURE.md    how the system fits together + why each piece is where it is
PLAN.md            roadmap and status (rewritten, not appended)
STATUS.md          implemented vs wanted, one page
BUGS.md            every known defect, severity, fix
IMPROVEMENTS.md    every improvement, by area, ranked
AGENT-DESIGN.md    the design philosophy: ground truth, cheap senses, bounded memory
HANDOFF-AUTOCLAW.md  the incident log and root causes from the original build

instabox/          machine deploy: docker-compose, .env.example, systemd, setup.sh
worker/            keep-alive Worker (cron 5m)
pages/public/      the proxy (_worker.js) + desktop chrome + status page
features/desktop/   lease-watcher, PTY server, systemd units, 3 harnesses
features/routines/  wake tick + pending prompts
features/groupchat/ Durable Object thread + machine-side relay
features/board/     ticket board (+ cost / open-work dashboards)

# ARCHITECTURE.md — how this system actually works

One page you can read in ten minutes and understand the whole deployment.
Everything else in `features/` is detail.

## 1. The problem this architecture solves

InstaBox Free gives you one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 20 GiB machine that **pauses
after 30 minutes idle**, has a **120-minute maximum run** (growing to 480 with
use), and cools down 5–135 minutes after a max-run pause. Cloudflare's free
tier fronts it. There is no always-on compute anywhere in the stack.

So the architecture is three layers that each do the one thing they are good
at:

```
        browser
           │  https://qwenpawx.pages.dev
           ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Cloudflare Pages + Workers  (always up)   │
│  • reverse proxy to the console           │
│  • auth gate / desktop lease / capabilities│
│  • keep-alive cron (5 min)                │
│  • routines, group chat, board, bot pages │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                   │ public port 8088 (a request here WAKES the box)
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ InstaBox Free machine (pauses when idle)  │
│  • QwenPaw container  :8088               │
│  • Xvfb :1 (Team)  + :2 (Private/QA)      │
│  • noVNC/view-only/terminal websockify    │
│  • computer-use MCP over SSE (8898/8897)  │
│  • lease-watcher (mirrors lease → control │
│    file the MCP proxy honors)             │
│  • Camoufox bridge (8899)                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Why a proxy and not just the InstaBox URL:** the box can be paused. Only a
Public-port request wakes it. The Pages proxy absorbs that: it retries once
after 45 s, and if the box is still booting it serves a self-refreshing
"waking up" page. The user never sees an InstaBox hostname.

**Why the keep-alive Worker:** QwenPaw's own scheduler (APScheduler cron jobs
in `jobs.json`) can only fire if the container is running. A 5-minute ping to
the public URL keeps the box awake as much as Free allows, and lets native
cron routines fire.

## 2. Auth model (this is the subtle part)

QwenPaw's auth is **header-based**: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or
`?token=`. There is **no cookie auth**. A plain browser navigation carries no
credential.

That collides with a proxy: the console is a SPA at `/`, the browser navigates
there with no header, and QwenPaw answers 401.

The solution is a two-stage handshake in `pages/public/_worker.js`:

1. `GET /` → proxy detects 401 → serves a **gate page** (HTML, our domain).
2. The gate page reads the token the console stored in `localStorage` from a
   previous login, POSTs it to `/desktop/__verify`, and the Worker mints an
   **HMAC-signed cookie** (`DESKTOP_SESSION`) scoped to our domain.
3. Every later `/desktop/*` request is authorized by that cookie.

**Never store a QwenPaw token in a cookie directly** — it is a bearer
credential with full console access. The HMAC cookie proves "this browser
completed a login recently" and expires on its own.

## 3. The desktop: view / control split + lease

The hard requirement: an agent and a human must share one screen without
fighting. Rakazo's model, ported here:

- **View** is free. `/desktop/session/view/<exp>.<cap>` → the view-only
  websockify port (6082 / 6084). Anyone logged in can watch.
- **Control** requires a **lease**: a 90-second grant, heartbeat-ed every 15 s
  while the page is visible, released explicitly or by expiry. Only one
  holder.
- **Control-only surfaces** (the interactive VNC port 6081, the terminal
  PTY 6083) are never reachable directly. They are served only through a
  **sealed capability**: AES-256-GCM, bound to `{mode, exp, generation,
  leaseId, computer}`, 60-minute TTL.

The lease is what the **MCP proxy honors**: `lease-watcher.py` (on the box)
polls the Worker every 5 s and writes `human worker-lease <epoch>` into
`/run/user/1000/instabox-control`. While that file exists and is fresh, the
computer-use MCP pro

# API key vault — the model can USE a key but never SEE it (Rakazo-style)

**Status: DEPLOYED + LIVE 2026-11-17 (D1 schema applied, master/broker
secrets provisioned, both Pages deployed, broker installed on the machine
at 172.18.0.1:8896, /health ready:true, /vault UI verified live in a real
browser with a canary item). Harnesses green: T106 55/55, T107 14/14, full
machine-free suite green. Live fixes during deploy: (1) broker port
8899 -> 8896 (8899 is the Camoufox bridge); (2) broker sends its own
User-Agent `QwenPaw-Vault-Broker/1.0` — Cloudflare blocks Python-urllib's

# Per-task cap design review (T126) — brief for DeepSeek

Context: QwenPaw v2.3.0 (AgentScope). ToolCallBudgetGate in
src/qwenpaw/loop/gates/limits.py enforces a PER-TURN cap at execution time
(try_reserve_execution, called from ReactAgent._execute_tool_call before the
first await): 30 total / 20 execute_shell_command per turn (reply_id-scoped),
refused calls yield a DENIED tool result. The gate's check() runs after each
model response and its TERMINATE is deferred. Live test 2026-11-18 proved it:
turn 1 executed 20 shell calls, but on the follow-up "hello" the agent resumed
the same echo-1-to-200 task and did 21-40. The per-turn counter resets on the
new reply_id, so the task can creep across turns.

## Proposed design (to be implemented in limits.py only; patch + config + mode wiring)

1. Per-TASK cap = 2x the per-turn cap: 60 total / 40 shell, cumulative across
   turns of one task. Rationale: one full turn plus one genuine resume turn;
   echo 1-200 needs 10 turns at 20/turn and stops at 40. Config fields
   task_max_calls / task_per_tool default to None / {} meaning "2x per-turn".
2. Task state lives ON the agent object (same place as the per-turn exec
   counter _tool_call_budget_exec), as _ToolCallTaskBudget: task_id,
   instruction (truncated starting user message), total + by_tool (EXECUTED
   calls, accumulated in try_reserve_execution on every successful reserve),
   max_calls / per_tool, finalized flag + reason. It is NOT reset when
   reply_id changes.
3. Task identity: explicit ctx["task_id"] / agent.state.task_id if present,
   else derived from the latest user message in agent.state.context.
   - No active task -> start one from the latest user message.
   - Active unfinalized task + continuation-only message (empty, greeting,
     "continue"/"go on"/"yes"/"ok"/"thanks") -> same task.
   - Active unfinalized task + a different substantive message -> new task
     (old abandoned, no fresh budget for repeats of the same instruction).
   - Finalized task + ANY substantive message (even a repeat) -> new task
     with a fresh budget. Finalized + continuation -> same finalized task.
4. Enforcement: try_reserve_execution checks the task cap BEFORE the per-turn
   cap; a refusal names the task total, records a stop-audit entry and
   finalizes the task. A successful reserve that brings the task total to
   exactly the cap finalizes the task immediately. The gate's check() also
   terminates on a finalized task (resume) or on task.total >= cap (safety
   net). A per-turn gate TERMINATE does NOT finalize the task (the task may
   legitimately continue next turn within its task budget); only the task
   cap finalizes.
5. Structured stop audit: append-only list on the agent
   (_tool_call_stop_audit), one record per stop, deduped per
   (task_id, turn/reply_id, kind): {ts ISO UTC, kind, reason, task_id,
   instruction, turn_id, turn_total, turn_executed, task_total, finalized}.
   Kinds: "per-turn gate" (gate check, per-turn), "per-task cap" (gate or
   enforcer, task total), "fuse" (enforcer refusal on per-turn grounds),
   "task_finalized" (a resumed turn on a finalized task). Accessors
   get_stop_audit(agent) / get_task_state(agent) return copies. Audit is
   in-memory for the chat session lifetime (agent object lifetime); no disk
   persistence in this change.
6. Fail-open: all task logic is wrapped so any exception (or a missing task
   API on old code) falls through to the existing per-turn behaviour; the
   per-turn gate reasons stay byte-identical (existing tests assert exact
   strings). The unreadable-batch edge (sub-calls bypassing the funnel, ~50)
   is NOT charged to the task total; documented as a remaining gap.

## Questions

A. Is storing task state on the agent object (not agent.state) sound for
   cross-turn persistence in AgentScope/QwenPaw, given the per-turn exec
   counter already lives there and reply_id changes per turn? What would
   break if the agent object were recreated per turn, and is there

# Loop-gate fix: make the tool-call budget actually enforce

## The bug (round 1: counting)

A custom loop mode "Guarded" used the built-in `ToolCallBudgetGate`
(`max_calls` 30, per-tool `execute_shell_command` 20). Two live tests
(echo 1–200, one echo per shell call) both executed **100 shell calls**
and stopped with "Tool call budget reached (100 calls)" / "(150 calls)"
— not 30 total, not 20 shell. The stored config was correct; the
running loop did not enforce it. The original incident was a 167-call
loop that ran ~6 minutes with no reply.

## Root cause, round 1 (read from the source, confirmed by the live log)

Two defects, both in the gate's counting:

1. **Double-counting via the merged message.** The parent AgentScope
   accumulates all of a turn's tool-call blocks into the assistant
   message(s) carrying the current `reply_id`
   (`state.append_context` merges blocks into the message with the
   current `reply_id`). The old gate read only the *latest* message
   with tool calls (`_latest_tool_names`) and **added** its names to
   the running total once per round. Because that message already held
   every call issued so far, the total inflated superlinearly:
   round 0 counted 50 (total 50), round 1 counted the accumulated 100
   (total 150), round 2 would count 150 (total 300). Live test 1
   fired at "(150 calls)" with 100 executed — exactly this.
2. **Stale `last_iteration` can skip a count.** The gate only counted
   when `iteration != state.last_iteration`. If the state was stale,
   a whole round was never counted. Live test 2 fired at
   "(100 calls)" instead of "(50 calls)", consistent with round 0
   not being counted.

A third, structural fact limits what any gate-only fix can do: the
model emits a large batch of parallel tool calls in one response
(~50–100), the gate only checks *after* the model response, and a
TERMINATE on a tool-call iteration is **deferred** (the triggering
batch still executes; the stop only prevents the next model call).
So a gate cannot enforce a bound below one batch.

## The bug (round 2: the workflow bypass)

The round-1 fix (image `qwenpaw-agentx:2.3.0-gatefix1`) was deployed
and live-tested in a fresh ordinary chat (echo 1–200). **The agent
reached 200 with NO budget stop.** It did not emit 200 direct tool
calls — it used the "Run workflow" batch runner (`run_tool_batch`):
4 batches of 50 (echo_batch*.json), turn header "Completed 15 steps"
(8 Thinking + 5 "Run workflow"). The gate counts only top-level tool
calls, so it saw 5 calls and never fired. The batch runner executes
its sub-calls internally (via `toolkit.call_tool`); those sub-calls
never appear as top-level tool-call blocks, so the gate was blind
to the workflow path.

## Root cause, round 2 (read from the source)

`run_tool_batch` (`qwenpaw/agents/tools/run_tool_batch.py`) reads a
JSON batch file (or inline `actions`, max 50 steps per invocation)
and executes each step through the toolkit. The parent appends both
the tool-call blocks and the tool-result blocks to the assistant
message(s) carrying the current `reply_id` (`AgentState.append_context`
merges every block into the message with the current `reply_id`, and
`_save_to_context` uses it for results too). So the sub-calls are
recoverable from the context — but only if the gate looks for them:
from the batch call's arguments (before it executes) and from the
batch result JSON (after it executes). The gatefix1 gate looked at
neither.

## The fix (round 2, image `qwenpaw-agentx:2.3.0-gatefix2`)

`qwenpaw-loop-gate-fix.patch` (against pinned upstream
`agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`, digest `sha256:46a782f4…`) changes three
files (the `mode.py` / `config.py` wiring is unchanged from round 1;
only `limits.py` changed):

- `src/qwenpaw/loop/gates/limits.py` — `ToolCallBudgetGate.check`
  now **recomputes** the turn total from the context on every check,
  scoped to the current reply (`agent.state.reply_id`): it counts
  every `tool_call`/`tool_use` block in every message w

# Multi-tab takeover (Step 10, 2026-11-19)

A non-owner tab of the same chat used to queue forever: the console's
single-sender ownership lock (`Web Lock qwenpaw:queue-owner:{chatUUID}`)
has no focus handoff, no timeout, and the "Interrupt & send" button is a
dead no-op in a non-owner tab (it returns early when the tab is not the
owner). The fix adds an explicit "Take over sending" action on the
queue-only banner.

## Mechanism (verified in the live bundle, image qwenpaw-agentx:2.3.0-approvalttl1)

Shared chunk `index-DZrIuh3B.js`: `$y()` is the singleton
`BroadcastChannel("qwenpaw:queue")`; `ar()` is `navigator.locks`;
`_q(e,t,n)` holds ownership with an exclusive lock request WITHOUT
`ifAvailable` (so it queues behind the owner) + `signal:n`; on grant it
calls become-owner, then waits until the signal aborts. The channel
listener handles `migrate`, `runState`, and generic item/runState sync;
a `release-ownership` message previously fell through to a no-op.

Chat chunk `index-opcB8AGu.js`: the hold effect creates a local
`AbortController o`, recovers the queue, then calls `Va(p, becomeOwner,
o.signal)`; cleanup aborts `o`. `pt` is the owner flag; `on = Xi && !pt`
renders the banner "This tab queues only; sending is handled by another
tab" (`chat.queue.otherTabOwner`).

## The patch (this image)

`apply-queue-takeover.py` does exact string surgery (the bundles are
minified, so unified diff cannot address a fragment mid-line), failing
closed unless every anchor occurs exactly once:

1. Shared chunk: the listener gains, before the `migrate` branch,
   `if (n.type === "release-ownership") { abort the controller in
   window.__agentxOwnerControllers for n.sessionId; return; }`.
2. Chat chunk hold effect: after `const o = new AbortController`,
   register `o` in `window.__agentxOwnerControllers` under `p` (the
   chat id); the effect cleanup deletes `p` (it already aborts `o`).

Aborting the owner's signal releases the lock, so the requester's
already-waiting hold is granted, `Zs(true)` hides the banner, and the
drain loop (`wq` = try-owner-then-send) drains the queue. Normal
single-tab behaviour is untouched: the registry is only read when a
`release-ownership` message arrives, which only the takeover button
posts.

## The injection (Pages `_worker.js`, rule `queue-takeover`)

When the "This tab queues only" banner is present on `/chat/<id>`, the
rule appends a "Take over sending" button to it (our element, recreated
on every rule run if React drops it); clicking posts
`{type: "release-ownership", sessionId}` on a fresh
`BroadcastChannel("qwenpaw:queue")` and disables itself as "Takeover
requested…". While the banner is up it hides the dead "Interrupt &
send" button (marked `data-agentx-interrupt-hidden`, restored when the
tab becomes owner). Until the patched image is deployed the button posts
a message the old bundle ignores — harmless.

## Takeover1 live failure + takeover2 (2026-11-19 ~09:1x IST)

The live two-tab browser test FAILED: the "Take over sending" button
rendered THREE times with independent state (truncated "Take over
sendi…"; clicking one set only that copy to "Takeover requested…") and

# Decision models — Jev (TypeSafe) and Drex (NACE)

**Status: Drex wired and ready, blocked on the NACE key.** Neither provider
has been called with a real key. Everything below is verified against a
local mock that implements the documented wire format, plus QwenPaw's own
provider source. T130 (21/21) covers the Drex wiring; T84 (33/33) still
covers the fail-closed client and the four integrations.

## What these are (and are not)

Both are **decision models**, not chat models. You send unstructured state plus
*typed questions* and get typed answers with probabilities, in 70–500 ms. There
is **no `/v1/chat/completions`**. Putting one in `active_model` or
`fallback_models` would 404 on every call — which is exactly the mistake the
NACE research warns about three separate ways.

| | Jev | Drex |
|---|---|---|
| Vendor | TypeSafe | NACE |
| Base | `https://api.typesafe.ai` | `https://console.nace.ai` |
| Model | `jev-latest` | `drex-max-v1.1` |
| Input | $0.042/MTok | **$0.03/MTok** |
| Output | never billed | never billed |
| Access | early access, key from console.typesafe.ai | key from console.nace.ai; 120 RPM free |
| Wire format | `POST /v1/systemone` | `POST /v1/systemone` (compatible) |

Because they share the wire format, **one client covers both**. That is not a
convenience: fallback logic, calibration and the audit trail are then written
once and cannot diverge between providers.

## The rule that matters

**No key, no call.** Every entry point fails closed:

- `decide()` raises `DecisionUnavailable` — it never returns a fabricated answer
- `decide_or_none()` returns `None` so a caller can fall back deliberately
- `is_enabled()` is `False`, so a feature can switch itself off
- `verdict_for_tool()`, `triage()`, `route_for_prompt()`, `should_wake()` all
  return `None` when unavailable

There is no simulated mode in a production path. A decision model that answers
without being asked is worse than one that is not installed.

## Safety default: low confidence never means "allow"

`verdict_for_tool()` sends the tool **name and arguments only** — never the
conversation. Sending a chat log to a third party to decide whether a shell
command is safe would leak more than it protects.

If the model answers `allow` with confidence below `0.7`, the verdict is
**coerced to `ask`**. A safety gate that fails open on uncertainty is not a
gate. Verified in the selftest.

## The four integrations

| Function | Question | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| `verdict_for_tool(name, args)` | allow / ask / deny | JEV approval level; overrides the DriverCard's blanket `allow` |
| `triage(message)` | urgent / routine / ignore | mailbox and group-chat routing |
| `route_for_prompt(prompt, routes)` | which of *our* route names | only when the lexical router in `features/routing/` abstained |
| `should_wake(reason)` | true / false | saves Free-tier run-minutes; a wrong `True` burns the day's allowance |

`route_for_prompt` is deliberately second in line: `features/routing/policy.py`
is free and lexical, this costs a call but understands paraphrase. Pay only
when the cheap one abstains.

## Calibration is not optional

"Calibrated probabilities" is the vendor's claim, not something this repo has
verified. `brier()` computes the Brier score (mean squared error of the
predicted probability) and `calibrate()` reports a verdict:

| Brier | Verdict |
|---|---|
| ≤ 0.10 | well calibrated on this sample |
| ≤ 0.20 | usable; keep the conservative threshold |
| ≤ 0.25 | barely better than guessing — prefer `ask` on safety paths |
| > 0.25 | **worse than guessing** — do not gate anything on this yet |

Collect `(predicted_probability, actual_outcome)` pairs from real verdicts and
run `calibrate()` before trusting any threshold. The default `0.7` is a
starting point, not a fact.

## Drex wiring (T130) — ready, blocked on the NACE key

What is wired, all in this directory:

- **`decide.py` — endpoint is configurable, not hardcoded.** Precedence:
  explicit `base=` argume

# Artifacts library — gap #14 (provisional T138)

An index, not new infrastructure. Walk a workspace directory plus
sent-file metadata plus history.db, store name / slug / date / size /
type / source in SQLite, and expose one searchable static page.
Backfill covers files that were sent before the index existed.

Built 2026-11-18. English only, no China endpoints, cloud LLM only,
InstaBox Free only. Stdlib-only Python, no network. Nothing on the
machine was modified; no container restart; no secrets in git.

## What already existed (verified, not assumed)

- **The open-work list already exists** (`features/board/README.md`
  #20: `open-work.html` + `refresh-open-work.py` + `follow-ups.md`,
  snapshot-based). It is **not** rebuilt here, and no live open-work
  feed is promised: snapshot + refresh is the ceiling on Free (no
  inbound route, Pages is static; near-live via Worker/D1 + cron is
  the best achievable and is out of scope here).
- The artifacts library itself did **not** exist: the board README
  records "no agent-produced artifacts yet, so the page lists recent
  workspace files instead". This feature is the library half of gap
  #14 only (evaluation `~/workspace/all-20-gaps-evaluation-2026-11-18.md`,
  gap #14 row + todo #7).

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `artifacts.py` | Indexer + search + backfill + page renderer (CLI) |
| `test_artifacts.py` | Machine-free test, provisional **T138 — 44/44** |
| `artifacts.html` | Shipped page (generated, 0 rows — regenerate on the machine) |
| `README.md` | This file |

## Usage

```bash
# Index a workspace (walk + optional backfill in one pass)
python3 artifacts.py index --workspace /data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/default \
    --db artifacts.db --history /data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/default/history.db \
    --sent-files sent.json

# Backfill only (files sent before the index existed)
python3 artifacts.py backfill --db artifacts.db \
    --workspace /data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/default \
    --sent-files sent.json --history .../history.db

# Search (JSON)
python3 artifacts.py search --db artifacts.db --query "report"

# Render the searchable page (static, works from any static host)
python3 artifacts.py render --db artifacts.db --out artifacts.html
```

Sent-file metadata is a JSON list of
`{"path": "rel/path.png", "sent_at": "...", "session_id": "...",
"channel": "console"}` records — one per file the agent already sent.
Only files that still exist under the workspace are indexed; a
missing file is skipped, not recorded.

## Schema (`artifacts` table in the index SQLite file)

`slug, name, path, date, size_bytes, type, source, session_id,
indexed_at`, with `UNIQUE (path, source)` and indexes on slug, type,
date, name. The idempotency key is `(path, source)`: re-indexing the
same file from the same source updates the row in place and never
creates a duplicate. A file can hold several rows — one per source
(e.g. `workspace` + `sent` + `history` for the same path).

  a second path with the same slug gets `-2`, `-3`, …
- **type:** from the extension (document / image / data /
  spreadsheet / presentation / code / audio / video / archive,
  else `other`).
- **date:** file mtime for workspace rows, `sent_at` for sent rows,
  the history row's `created_at` for history rows.
- **source:** `workspace` (walk), `sent` (sent-file metadata),
  `history` (path mentioned in history.db content).

  actually exist on disk (a path regex cannot see spaces in names
  like "Meeting Notes.md", so the matcher checks each real workspace
  file's relative path / name against the content). No m

# Cost ledger with a hard kill switch (gap #5, research §2 gap 10)

## The problem

`token_usage.json` exists and is read — but it is read-only telemetry with
no spend limit at all (verified in `features/approvals/README.md`: grep for
`spend|budget|cap` over `token_usage/*.py` and `config.py` returns nothing;
there is no hook that reads usage before a call and refuses it). Own keys +
cloud-only + fallback chains = a runaway loop can burn real money overnight.
Tool-call caps do not bound tokens: one giant context per call is unbounded
(the loop-gate bounds calls, not tokens).

## What this builds

A real ledger plus a cap, in `features/cost-ledger/`:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `cost_ledger.py` | The implementation. Stdlib only; loads standalone. Also the file the patch installs as `qwenpaw/token_usage/cost_ledger.py` (byte-identical to `src/patched/cost_ledger.py`). |
| `cost_server.py` | Reference `/cost` server (stdlib `http.server`). Runnable spec, not the deployed endpoint. |
| `cost-prices.json` | Static price table (USD per 1M tokens). Sync to the machine as `working/cost-prices.json`. |
| `cost-budget.json` | Default budget. Sync to the machine as `working/cost-budget.json`. |
| `qwenpaw-cost-ledger.patch` | Derived-image patch (loop-gate-fix pattern). |
| `Dockerfile` | Builds `qwenpaw-agentx:2.3.0-costledger1` from `bloatwinwin1`. |
| `test_cost_ledger.py` | T125, machine-free, 55 checks. |
| `src/pristine/` | Exact upstream v2.3.0 files the patch touches (`model_wrapper.py`, `app/routers/__init__.py`), sha256-verified against `~/workspace/qwenpaw-src` (v2.3.0, release-note commit `0a21644`). |
| `src/patched/` | Patched files + the two new files (`cost_ledger.py`, `cost.py`). The patch is the diff between these two trees and was verified to apply cleanly (`-p1` and `-p2`) and reproduce the patched files byte-for-byte. |

## The ledger format

The ledger reads the EXISTING `token_usage.json` format and never changes
it — the file is the source of truth. Top-level keys are dates; each maps
an `"agent\x1fprovider\x1fmodel"` key (`\x1f` = unit separator) to
`{provider_id, model_name, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens,
cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, call_count, agent_id}`.

Billing rules (stated, not hidden):

- Billable input = `prompt_tokens` ONLY. `cache_read_tokens` /
  `cache_write_tokens` are a SUBSET of `prompt_tokens` (see
  `token_usage/manager.py` `_cache_usage_metrics`: the cache-eligible
  denominator IS `prompt_tokens` for non-Anthropic providers), so adding
  them would double-count. They are reported, never billed. (T125 A13:
  10,000 prompt with 8,000 cache-read bills $0.01, not $0.018.)
- Billable output = `completion_tokens`.
- Cost = input/1M × input price + output/1M × output price, priced by
  `provider:model` first, then by model name alone.
- A model with no price has cost `None` (unpriced) — its TOKENS still
  count, and the token budget still binds it. The TOTAL cost figures are
  the sum over PRICED models (a lower bound when unpriced models exist);
  `*_cost_known: false` means the total is partial, not unknown. (This
  was a real bug the post-implementation DeepSeek review caught: the
  first version returned `None` for the whole day's USD whenever ANY
  model was unpriced, which disabled the USD cap entirely.)
- "Per-run" in the ledger = the current process run, tracked in memory
  by the gate (`run_prompt_tokens`, `run_completion_tokens`, `run_cost_usd`,
  `run_calls`, reported as `current_run` by `/cost`). The file itself has
  no run id — it aggregates by (date, agent, provider, model) — so
  per-day and cumulative are what the file can prove; per-run is what the
  live gate counted since process start.

## The price table

`cost-prices.json`, USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Static only — no price is
ever fetched from the network (T125 E1/E2: no `httpx`/`requests`/
`urllib.request`/`urlopen` anywhere in the ledger, server, or router, and
no URL in the price file).

| `src/pristine/` | Exact upstream v2.3.0 files the patch touches (`model_wrapper.py`, `app/routers/__init__.py`), sha256-verified against `~/workspace/qwenpaw-src` (v2.3.0, release-note commit `0a21644`). |
| `src/patched/` | Patched files + the two new files (`cost_ledger.py`, `cost.py`). The patch is the diff between these two trees and was verified to apply cleanly (`-p1` and `-p2`) and reproduce the patched files byte-for-byte. |

## The ledger format

The ledger reads the EXISTING `token_usage.json` format and never changes
it — the file is the source of truth. Top-level keys are dates; each maps
an `"agent\x1fprovider\x1fmodel"` key (`\x1f` = unit separator) to
`{provider_id, model_name, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens,
cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, call_count, agent_id}`.

Billing rules (stated, not hidden):

- Billable input = `prompt_tokens` ONLY. `cache_read_tokens` /
  `cache_write_tokens` are a SUBSET of `prompt_tokens` (see
  `token_usage/manager.py` `_cache_usage_metrics`: the cache-eligible
  denominator IS `prompt_tokens` for non-Anthropic providers), so adding
  them would double-count. They are reported, never billed. (T125 A13:
  10,000 prompt with 8,000 cache-read bills $0.01, not $0.018.)
- Billable output = `completion_tokens`.
- Cost = input/1M × input price + output/1M × output price, priced by
  `provider:model` first, then by model name alone.
- A model with no price has cost `None` (unpriced) — its TOKENS still
  count, and the token budget still binds it. The TOTAL cost figures are
  the sum over PRICED models (a lower bound when unpriced models exist);
  `*_cost_known: false` means the total is partial, not unknown. (This
  was a real bug the post-implementation DeepSeek review caught: the
  first version returned `None` for the whole day's USD whenever ANY
  model was unpriced, which disabled the USD cap entirely.)
- "Per-run" in the ledger = the current process run, tracked in memory
  by the gate (`run_prompt_tokens`, `run_completion_tokens`, `run_cost_usd`,
  `run_calls`, reported as `current_run` by `/cost`). The file itself has
  no run id — it aggregates by (date, agent, provider, model) — so
  per-day and cumulative are what the file can prove; per-run is what the
  live gate counted since process start.

## The price table

`cost-prices.json`, USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Static only — no price is
ever fetched from the network (T125 E1/E2: no `httpx`/`requests`/
`urllib.request`/`urlopen` anywhere in the ledger, server, or router, and
no URL in the price file).

# Per-chat thinking selector

A visible Thinking selector in the chat UI, next to the composer
controls — **Default / Off / Low / Medium / High / XHigh** — stored per
chat. User request, 2026-11-18: "add thinking mode per chat enable
disable option xhigh hig,, low medium like i ncoding agent".

## The backend already had it

QwenPaw supports per-chat thinking end to end (verified against the
live container source, not a note):

- `qwenpaw/providers/thinking.py`: `ThinkingLevel` = inherit / off /
  minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh / max / budget.
  `ThinkingPreference` = `{level, budget_tokens?}` (budget_tokens is
  required iff level == "budget").
- `qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py`: `GET /chats/{chat_id}/thinking` and
  `PUT /chats/{chat_id}/thinking` (mounted under `/api`, so the full
  path is `/api/chats/{id}/thinking`). GET returns a view with
  `value.level` (the stored per-chat level), `effective`, `control`
  (kind/efforts/supports_off), `model_key` and `reason`. PUT takes a
  `ThinkingPreference` body, optional `?model_key=`; 409 when the model
  changed since the GET, 422 when the level is invalid for the current
  model. It persists for subsequent turns of THIS session only.
- `GET /api/chats/thinking-default` exposes the agent default for a
  not-yet-created session.

Nothing on the machine was changed. The selector is a pure UI surface
over this API, injected by the `thinking-selector` rule in
`pages/public/_worker.js`.

## How the rule works

- Anchor: the chat composer toolbar itself — the Smart Mode row, the
  parent of the "Smart Mode" button (user screenshot, 2026-11-19: the
  selector sits in the circled toolbar next to Smart Mode, in the chat,
  not in Settings → General). Fallbacks: the parent of the "Context
  usage" button, then the chat input's grandparent. Only on `/chat*`
  pages.
- It appends (never moves) a "Thinking" label + a native `<select>`
  into the toolbar. React owns the toolbar, so the rule re-creates the
  select on every observer run if React removed it; the select is our
  own element, so re-creating it cannot break React reconciliation
  (the round-17 lesson: no moving text nodes, no wrapping).
- On a chat change it GETs `/api/chats/{id}/thinking` with
  `Authorization: Bearer <qwenpaw_auth_token>` (localStorage, same as
  the Your Keys fix) and shows `value.level`. A second run on the same
  chat fetches nothing.
- On change it PUTs `{level}` with the `model_key` from the last GET
  (the 409 guard). A 409 or 422 re-syncs from the server and reverts
  the select to the stored level. A GET 401 (no token) is a safe no-op.
- A level outside the offered set (minimal/max/budget) is shown by
  adding an option for it, so the select never displays a wrong value.
- Brand-new chat (no id yet): a pick is stored as pending in
  localStorage (`agentx_thinking_pending`) with no fetch, and PUT once
  the first message creates the chat and the URL gains an id. The
  first turn of a brand-new chat therefore still uses the default;
  the second turn uses the pick. (Injecting
  `request_context.session_thinking` into the SPA's first message
  would need hooking the SPA's own fetch — too invasive; the pending
  apply is the safe approach.)

## Quota

Cost is proportional to user action, never to wall clock (AGENTS.md
§6): one GET per chat change, one PUT per user pick. No polling, no
timer, no per-tick fetch. The rule runs on the existing
MutationObserver only.

`features/test-project/run-tests.py`): static checks on the real

Bearer from localStorage, the six options, model_key, no polling,
appendChild-only) + dynamic checks with a DOM mock and a fetch mock
(create in the Smart Mode row, PUT on change, no duplicate GET/select,
pending on a new chat, 422 revert, out-of-set level shown truthfully,
401 no-op, off-chat no-op). Fail-first proven: 21/23 fail against the
pre-feature `_worke

# Feature #15 — Model fallbacks + per-bot model + thinking level

## Status: PROPOSAL ONLY — nothing applied

This file proposes an exact, verified change. It is **not** applied.
Applying needs the user's OK, and it is applied through QwenPaw's own
API (which validates the slots and reloads the agent) — never by editing
files on the machine, and with no container restart.

## What was verified live (2026-11-15, machine m_agq5wqqo2fvypym7rjlpvngc2m)

### 1. QwenPaw DOES support an ordered fallback chain — per agent

Source (inside container `qwenpaw`, image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`):

- `/app/src/qwenpaw/config/config.py:2564` — `AgentConfig.fallback_models:
  List[ModelSlotConfig]`, described as
  "Ordered chat model fallback chain for transient failures".
- `/app/src/qwenpaw/config/config.py:204` — `ModelSlotConfig` is exactly
  `{provider_id: str, model: str}`. Nothing else.
- `/app/src/qwenpaw/config/config.py:2275` — `FallbackPolicyConfig` is
  `{enabled: bool = True, target_scope: "configured" | "free_only"}`.
- `/app/src/qwenpaw/config/config.py:2550` — `AgentConfig` also carries
  `active_model`, `decision_model`, `subagent_model`, `thinking_level`,
  `thinking_budget`, `llm_routing`.
- `/app/src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py:2357,2409-2488` —
  `_apply_model_fallbacks()` reads `agent_config.fallback_models` and
  builds an ordered `FallbackChatModel([primary, *fallbacks])`. It
  **skips** any slot whose provider is missing/disabled, whose model is
  unknown, or which duplicates the primary; with `target_scope:
  "free_only"` it also skips non-free models. Fallback models get
  `max_retries = 0`. If only the primary survives, no fallback wrapper
  is built.
- `/app/src/qwenpaw/providers/fallback_chat_model.py:39-40` —
  "Try configured models in order before any response becomes visible."
- `/app/src/qwenpaw/app/routers/agents.py:1353` — `PATCH
  /api/agents/{agentId}/model-settings` patches exactly these fields
  (`AgentModelSettingsPatch`: `active_model`, `decision_model`,
  `fallback_models`, `fallback_policy`, `subagent_model`,
  `thinking_level`, `thinking_budget`). It validates every slot with
  `validate_model_slot()` (unknown/disabled model → HTTP 422, nothing
  applied) and then triggers an agent reload. No restart needed.

### 2. Where the settings live (this is the part Astra-style guesses get wrong)

- Fallbacks/thinking level live **per agent** in the workspace file
  `working/workspaces/<agent>/agent.json` (`AgentProfileConfig`).
  They do **NOT** live in `working/config.json`: that file has no
  `providers`, no `fallback` key (grep count 0), and its
  `agents.profiles.<id>` entries only carry `id/workspace_dir/enabled/
  pinned`. The `agents.llm_routing` block in `config.json` is a
  different feature (see §5).
- The **primary model is global**, not per agent:
  `working.secret/providers/active_model.json` currently reads
  `{"provider_id": "xingchiapi", "model": "gpt-6-astra"}`. Both agents'
  `agent.json` files have `active_model: null`, so both use that global
  model today. (Memory said Kilo was active; the user switched to GPT
  Astra in the console on 2026-11-15 — verified live, see cost page.)
- Current per-agent state (read live from both `agent.json` files):
  `fallback_models: []`, `fallback_policy: {"enabled": true,
  "target_scope": "configured"}`, `thinking_level: "inherit"`.

InstaBox Free only. Nothing on the machine was modified; no container
restart; no secrets in git.

## #12 — Ticket board (LIVE)

- **URL:** https://qwenpaw-board.qwenpaw-rohan.workers.dev
- **Worker:** `qwenpaw-board` (Cloudflare account
  `ca85fe3692c3f378200950999df9a35e`, subdomain `qwenpaw-rohan`)
- **Storage:** D1 database `qwenpaw-state`
  (`5f58a2f8-e4bb-45e5-8a94-4fc283b90871`) — table `tickets`, one row
  per ticket (migrated 2026-11-15; see "Board v3 (D1)" below). KV
  namespace `qwenpaw-board-tickets`
  (`90508a020d27455b83d137f8c0323774`) is kept as the **fallback only**
  (`USE_D1="0"`); `/health` reports which store is live
  (`"store":"d1"`).
- **Rate limiting:** Durable Object `BoardRateLimiter` (see "Rate
  limiting" below) — failed-auth attempts capped at 30/min/IP,
  authenticated mutations at 30/min/IP + 1,000/day/IP; over-cap →
  429 with `Retry-After`. Fixes audit bug `board-no-rate-limit-auth`.
- **Source:** `worker/src/index.js` (no build step),
  `worker/wrangler.toml` (reference; deploys were done via the
  Cloudflare API, see below), `features/board/worker/harness-board.mjs` (67 checks:
  CRUD round trip, all audit fixes, DO rate-limit buckets, D1-down →
  503, KV fallback).
- **Auth:** shared board key in the Worker secret `BOARD_TOKEN`. Every
  `/api/*` call needs it as `?key=` or `X-Board-Key` header. The HTML
  page asks for it once and stores it in `localStorage`. The key value
  is **not** in this repo — ask the coordinator for it.
- **Columns:** To do / In progress / In review / Blocked / Done / Won't do
  (6 columns, matching Rakazo's board exactly).
- **API:** `GET /api/tickets`, `POST /api/tickets`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE
  /api/tickets/:id`, `POST /api/tickets/:id/comments`,
  `POST /api/tickets/:id/mark-sent`,
  `GET /api/tickets/:id/qwenpaw-task`, `GET /health`.
- **Comments:** tickets carry a `comments` list (max 50, 1000 chars each);
  comments are included in the QwenPaw task text. (Rakazo parity:

- **Mark as sent:** after posting a ticket to QwenPaw, `POST

# Build Page

Build a single self-contained HTML page and publish it to Cloudflare
Pages, then give the user the public URL.

## Rules

- **English only.** All page text, labels and comments in English.
- **Self-contained.** One HTML file per page: inline CSS in `<style>`,
  inline JavaScript in `<script>` if needed. No external fonts, scripts,
  images or trackers. No server, no database, no form that posts anywhere.
- **No China endpoints or services.** No links, embeds or assets from
  Chinese domains or providers.
- **Never print, log or paste the Cloudflare API token.** It arrives as
  the `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` environment variable. If it is missing, stop
  and tell the user to set it (see "Token setup" below) instead of
  guessing or asking for the token in chat.
- **Every deployment is a full snapshot.** Deploying replaces the whole
  `qwenpaw-pages` project, so always deploy the complete pages directory,
  never a single file on its own.
- **Keep a 404 page.** `<workspace>/pages/404.html` must always exist
  (copy it from `features/botpages/404.html` in the repo if it is
  missing). Cloudflare Pages serves it with a real 404 for unknown URLs;
  without it, any typo'd URL returns the homepage with HTTP 200. Never
  delete it when deploying.

## Workflow

### 1. Agree the page with the user

Confirm the slug (URL path), title and the content. A slug is lowercase
letters, digits and hyphens only, e.g. `launch-party`. The page will be
live at `https://qwenpaw-pages.pages.dev/<slug>/`.

### 2. Write the page

Write the page to `<workspace>/pages/<slug>/index.html`, where
`<workspace>` is the current agent's workspace directory. Keep all bot
pages in that one `pages/` directory so step 4 always deploys everything
together. The workspace homepage is `<workspace>/pages/index.html`.

Page requirements:

- Valid HTML, `<html lang="en">`, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, a viewport
  meta tag, a `<title>`, and a visible heading.
- Readable on a phone: responsive layout, no fixed pixel widths wider
  than the screen.
- Keep the file under 1 MB.

### 3. Get the deploy script

The deploy script lives in the public repo and needs no token to fetch:

```bash
mkdir -p <workspace>/pages-deploy
curl -fsSL -o <workspace>/pages-deploy/deploy-page.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ratulbaba7/qwenpaw-deploy/main/features/botpages/deploy-page.py
```

Re-fetch it if it is older than the repo's current version. Do not edit
the script; if it fails, report the exact error to the user.

### 4. Deploy the whole pages directory

```bash
python3 <workspace>/pages-deploy/deploy-page.py <workspace>/pages \
  --project=qwenpaw-pages --branch=main
```

The script prints the deployment id and URL. Wait for it to finish and
check that it reports success. If it fails, do not retry blindly: read
the error, fix the cause (usually a bad file type or an oversized file),
and deploy again.

### 5. Verify and report

Fetch the live URL and confirm it returns HTTP 200 and contains the
page title. Also fetch a nonsense URL (e.g. `/does-not-exist-xyz/`) and
confirm it returns 404: if it returns 200, `404.html` is missing from
the pages directory — add it (see Rules) and redeploy. Then reply to
the user with:

- the public URL (`https://qwenpaw-pages.pages.dev/<slug>/`)
- one line saying what the page is
- the workspace path of the source file, so they can ask for edits

For an edit, change the file in `<workspace>/pages/<slug>/index.html`
and repeat steps 4-5.

## Token setup (for the user, done once)

The dep

# Bot-built shareable Pages (#7)

QwenPaw can build a web page from a chat request and publish it as a
shareable public URL. This folder holds the skill, the deploy script, and
a sample page. Live project: **qwenpaw-pages**
(`https://qwenpaw-pages.pages.dev/`).

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `build-page-SKILL.md` | Source copy of the `build-page` skill installed on the machine (see "Installed" below). |
| `deploy-page.py` | Deploys a directory of static pages to a Cloudflare Pages project via the direct-upload API. |
| `sample-page.html` | Sample page deployed to the project root on 2026-11-15 (verified HTTP 200). |
| `404.html` | Custom 404 page. Cloudflare Pages serves it with a real HTTP 404 for unknown URLs. Without it, every unknown URL returned the homepage with HTTP 200 (found by live test 2026-11-15) — which also made the skill's "verify 200" check meaningless. Deployed 2026-11-15; unknown paths now return 404. Keep this file in every future snapshot of the project (the `build-page` skill now says so). |

## Installed (on the machine)

- `working/skill_pool/build-page/SKILL.md` — shared skill pool
- `working/workspaces/default/skills/build-page/SKILL.md` — default workspace

Both copies are identical. Registered with QwenPaw's own reconcile
(`qwenpaw skills list --pool` / `qwenpaw skills list` inside the
container); the pool manifest lists it with `source: "customized"`.

## How it works

1. The user asks for a page ("make a page for the launch party").
2. The agent writes one self-contained HTML file to
   `<workspace>/pages/<slug>/index.html` (English only, inline CSS/JS,
   no external resources, no trackers, no China endpoints).
3. The agent fetches the deploy script from this public repo:
   `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ratulbaba7/qwenpaw-deploy/main/features/botpages/deploy-page.py`
4. The agent runs it over the whole pages directory:
   `python3 deploy-page.py <workspace>/pages --project=qwenpaw-pages --branch=main`
5. The agent verifies the URL returns HTTP 200 and gives the user the link:
   `https://qwenpaw-pages.pages.dev/<slug>/`

## Deploy script

`deploy-page.py <source-dir> [--project=qwenpaw-pages] [--branch=main]`

- Uses the Wrangler direct-upload protocol, the same flow as the proven
  `scripts/deploy-pages-proxy.py`: upload-token JWT, blake3 file hashes,
  check-missing, upload missing files, upsert-hashes, create deployment.
- Accepts only `.html/.css/.js/.json/.txt/.svg/.png/.jpg/.webp/.ico`
  files, max 20 MB per file. Special files (`_worker.js`, `_headers`,
  `_redirects`, `_routes.json`) are skipped.
- **Every deployment is a full snapshot of the project.** Always deploy
  the complete pages directory; deploying one file alone would delete
  every other page.
- Auth: `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` env var first (a token with the
  "Cloudflare Pages: Edit" scope); if unset, falls back to the Muse
  Cloudflare connector credential surrogate when run from this VM.
  Never put a real token in the file or in git. The script never prints
  a token or JWT.
- Account id defaults to `ca85fe3692c3f378200950999df9a35e`
  (`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` overrides it).

## One-time setup (user)

1. Create the project once (done 2026-11-15):
   `python3 cf.py post /client/v4/accounts/<id>/pages/projects '{"name":"qwenpaw-pages","production_branch":"main"}'`
2. Create a Cloudflare API token with "Cloudflare Pages: Edit" and store
   it in QwenPaw's encrypted env store (run inside the container):
   `qwenpaw env set CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN <token>`
   Until this is set, the skill can write pages but cannot publish them.

## Verified live (2026-11-15)

- Project `qwenpaw-pages` created; subdomain `qwenpaw-pages.pages.dev`.
- `deploy-page.py` run end-to-end from this repo against the live API:
  deployed the sample page (`/`) and the skill-library page (`/skills/`)
  in one deployment.
- `https://qwenpaw-pages.pages.dev/` → HTTP 200, sample page.
- `https://qwenpaw-pages.pages.dev/skills/` → HTTP 200, skill

# Memory (Phase 4) — bounded recall, lessons ledger, ReMe doctor

Three stdlib-only Python tools. No new index, no embeddings, no LLM call,
no third-party dependency. Everything here is read-only with respect to
QwenPaw's data.

## Read this first: what already exists upstream

QwenPaw **v2.3.0 already ships full-text history recall.** Verified against
the real source on 2026-11-15:

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/memoryspace.py` → `MemorySpace.search()`
  over an external-content FTS5 table
  `conversation_history_fts` (tokenize `porter unicode61`) on
  `conversation_history`, with SQLite progress-handler timeouts.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/recall_tool.py` → the agent-facing
  `recall_history` tool (`op="search"|"expand"|"recall_tool"|"days_between"`),
  including the equivalent of `fts_match_query()` and a LIKE fallback for
  builds without FTS5.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_config.py` deliberately scopes ReMe to
  `daily_dir` + `digest_dir` **markdown only**, with an explicit comment
  that raw conversation lookup belongs to `recall_history(op="search")`.

So the plan's "Tier 1 FTS5 recall bridge" would have **duplicated working
code**. What upstream's tool does *not* do is what this directory adds:

| Gap | Upstream | Here |
|---|---|---|
| Budget unit | rows (1000) / bytes (4 MB) | **tokens (2,000 hard cap)** |
| Result count | `k` default 10 | **3 hard default, 10 absolute max** |
| Credential safety | none | **redaction at read time** |
| Runs outside the agent loop | no (in-process tool) | **yes (host CLI)** |
| Lessons workflow | none | **candidate/accept ledger** |
| "Why is memory empty?" | none | **5-cause doctor** |

Use upstream `recall_history` **inside** a conversation. Use these tools
**outside** it, or when the token budget and redaction matter.

## `recall.py` — bounded recall

```bash
python3 recall.py --db /data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/default/history.db \
  --query "desktop lease" --limit 3

python3 recall.py --db ... --query "KV quota" --agent default \
  --since 2026-11-15 --json

python3 recall.py --db ... --check        # schema + FTS5 probe only
```

Guarantees, all covered by `test_recall.py`:

- **≤ 3 results by default**, ≤ 10 with `--limit`, never a whole session —
  every hit is a window of ≤ 600 chars around the first matching term.
- **≤ 2,000 tokens** per call. `ABSOLUTE_BUDGET_TOKENS = 2000` cannot be
  raised by a flag; asking for more is an error, not a clamp.
- **Empty is a valid answer.** With a tiny budget you get zero hits and
  `truncated_by_budget: true` rather than a maimed excerpt.
- **Redaction** of GitHub PATs, `sk-*`, AWS key ids, Slack, JWTs, bearer
  headers, `*token*/secret/password/api_key = ...` assignments, and long
  hex blobs. Reported as `redactions_applied`.
- **Tool-result rows excluded by default** (~65% of rows are tool noise);
  `--include-tool-results` opts in.
- **Read-only**, enforced twice: `mode=ro` URI plus an SQLite authorizer
  that denies every mutation.
- **Self-pollution guard**: rows whose `name` is `recall_history` /
  `recall_history_python` are skipped, mirroring upstream's FTS exclusion.

### One subtlety worth knowing

An external-content FTS5 table reads its own configuration from
`sqlite_master` through a `SQLITE_UPDATE` code path when the vtab connects.
A naive "deny all UPDATE" authorizer makes every FTS query fail with
`vtable constructor failed`. The authorizer therefore denies mutations for
every object **except** `sqlite_master`; `mode=ro` remains the real
guarantee. `test_recall.py` covers both halves (FTS works *and* writes are
denied).

## `lessons.py` — the lessons ledger

Operates on the **existing** `## Important Decisions and Lessons` section of
`MEMORY.md` (no new file — the plan says so, and MEMORY.md is already read
whole at task start).

```bash
python3 lessons.py --file MEMORY.md list
python3 lessons.py --file MEMORY.md check

# propose is the ONLY thing the agent may do unattended:
python3 lessons.

# Memory — compact facts + session handoff

You have a memory that costs few tokens and is fast to search. It is
**not** the whole conversation history. The full history stays in
`history.db` (never modified, never deleted) and is searchable on demand.
This skill is the compact layer on top of it: distilled facts plus a
session handoff, so a new session can continue where the last one left
off instead of starting cold.

## The tools (all read `memory.db`, a NEW file — never history.db)

All commands run on the machine (you are inside the QwenPaw container).
The store lives at `/app/working/workspaces/default/memory.db`
and the CLI at `/app/working/memory-tools/facts.py`.
(These are the in-container paths: the host directory
`/data/home/qwenpaw/working` is mounted at `/app/working`.)

```bash
DB=/app/working/workspaces/default/memory.db
CLI=/app/working/memory-tools/facts.py
HIST=/app/working/workspaces/default/history.db

# start of a session: what did the last session leave?
python3 $CLI --db $DB handoff-read
# retrieve only the facts relevant to the current topic (a few hundred tokens)
python3 $CLI --db $DB search --query "<topic>" --limit 5
# search everything (facts + the full history, read-only)
python3 $CLI --db $DB search-history --history $HIST --query "<topic>" --limit 3
# propose candidate facts from a transcript (proposes only, never writes)
python3 $CLI --db $DB extract --transcript /tmp/turns.txt --session <id>
# add a fact you judged salient (entities are auto-extracted from the
# text when you do not supply them — people, projects, quoted names).
# Route EVERY add through the durable-write gate, NOT `facts.py add`:
# high-stakes facts (preferences, identity, credentials-adjacent
# mentions, "from now on" language) are HELD for explicit accept and
# never land unattended; routine facts write silently with provenance.
# `facts.py add` is the raw low-level path — do not call it directly.
python3 /app/working/memory-tools/durable_write.py --db $DB add-gated \
    --text "<one sentence>" --kind decision --session <id> --importance 3
# a held fact waits in the pending store until it is confirmed:
python3 /app/working/memory-tools/durable_write.py --db $DB list
python3 /app/working/memory-tools/durable_write.py --db $DB accept \
    --id PF-001 --why "user confirmed"
# what was true on a past date? (time travel: facts valid then)
python3 $CLI --db $DB search --query "<topic>" --as-of 2026-11-15 --limit 5
# end of a session: write the handoff for the next session
python3 $CLI --db $DB handoff-write --session <id> --summary "<one or two sentences>" \
    --open-tasks '["First open task", "Second open task"]' \
    --left-off "<where this session stopped, in one sentence>"
```

If a command fails because a file is missing, say so and stop — do not
invent a path. Do not write to `history.db`, `working.secret/auth.json`,
or any user chat.

`search` for the topic at hand. That is the whole context you

approvals — both replace, not merge). The rest are documented limits.

loops and destructive mistakes is acting before understanding — so the

You are in plan mode. Your job is to **understand first, change nothing**.

  rejected. Run: `python3 features/plan-mode/plan_mode.py exit`
  The draft plan file stays on disk as a record; it is never executed
  after an exit.

  (or running `python3 features/plan-mode/plan_mode.py approve

  and no approval by silence.

Allowed — read-only only:

- Read files, list directories, search the codebase (`grep`, `glob`).
- Read the web (`web_search`, `web_fetch`) and read memory

- Read git state (`git status`, `git log`, `git diff`).
- Run read-only shell commands: `ls`, `cat`, `grep`, `git status`.
