# Cloudflare Code Mode — research note

Source: `cloudflare/agents` repo (cloned 2026-11-15, `main`, package
`@cloudflare/codemode` v0.5.6). Status in repo: **Experimental — may have
breaking changes. Use with caution in production.** (README header.)

Local clone for reference: `~/workspace/research/cloudflare-agents/`

## 1. What Code Mode is

Instead of the model calling tools one at a time, the model gets **one tool**
(`codemode({ code })`) and writes TypeScript/JavaScript that orchestrates
many operations inside a sandboxed Worker. The repo's own summary: "LLMs are
better at writing code than calling tools — they've seen millions of lines of
real-world code but only contrived tool-calling examples."

Two layers, do not confuse them:

| Layer | What it is | Token behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Legacy `createCodeTool`** (`@cloudflare/codemode/ai`, `createCodeTool({ tools, executor })`) | Generates TypeScript types from your tool providers and builds ONE AI-SDK tool whose description contains the full type block (`{{types}}` replaced by the generated types — verified in `packages/codemode/src/tool.ts:102-117`). The model writes an `async () => {...}` function calling `codemode.toolName(args)`. | All tool schemas ARE still in the prompt (same as classic tool calling). Savings come only from fewer round trips, not from a smaller prompt. Also `resolveProvider` **filters out** tools with `needsApproval` instead of pausing (verified `tool.ts:82-89`). |
| **Runtime `createCodemodeRuntime`** (`createCodemodeRuntime({ ctx, executor, connectors })`, `runtime.tool()`) | Durable engine on a Durable Object facet. Connectors are classes (MCP / OpenAPI / AI-SDK toolset / custom). The model discovers tools **inside the sandbox** via `codemode.search(query)` / `codemode.describe(target)`; results return into the running code, **not into the context window** (verified `docs/codemode/runtime.md`). The tool description carries only short per-connector hints, not full schemas (verified `packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts`). | This is the path that actually shrinks the prompt. |

### The sandbox SDK (what the model writes)

```ts
async () => {
  const matches = await codemode.search("open pull requests");   // discover
  const docs = await codemode.describe(matches.results[0].path); // learn, on demand
  const prs = await github.list_pull_requests({ owner, repo, state: "open" }); // act
  const stamp = await codemode.step("now", () => Date.now());    // do-once (replay-safe)
  return { count: prs.length, stamp };
};
// reuse: const prs = await codemode.run("open-prs", { owner, repo });
```

### How the code runs

1. `createCodeTool` / `runtime.tool()` builds the tool; the LLM writes an async
   arrow function (AST-normalised via acorn, markdown fences stripped).
2. `DynamicWorkerExecutor` spins up an isolated Worker via a **Worker Loader**
   binding (`env.LOADER`), one `ToolDispatcher` per namespace; calls route back
   via Workers RPC through a `Proxy` per namespace.
3. Console output is captured and returned with the result.
4. **Network isolation: external `fetch()` / `connect()` are blocked by default**
   (`globalOutbound: null`, enforced at the Workers runtime level). Controlled
   outbound access only by passing a `Fetcher` as `globalOutbound`.
5. Default execution timeout **60,000 ms** (`DEFAULT_DYNAMIC_WORKER_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS`,
   `packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:261`), configurable via `timeout` option.
   The `Executor` interface is minimal and replaceable (Node VM, QuickJS,
   containers) — `DynamicWorkerExecutor` is just the Workers implementation.

### Connectors

- **`McpConnector`** — wraps an MCP connection; each MCP tool becomes one
  method on the connector namespace (`github.list_pull_requests(...)`).
  Fetches tools via `listTools()`, dispatches via
  `connection.client.callTool()`; tool names sanitised to valid JS identifiers
  (verified `packages/codemode/src/connectors/mcp.ts`). The `tool(name, t)`
  hook decorates

Private :2, bridge + Camoufox, computer-use MCP, routines, group chat,

# QwenPaw test results (RESULTS.md)

Every full or partial run of the test project is recorded here as a
**round**. The runner (`run-tests.py`) appends Round 1, 2, 3, … itself.
Browser / needs-token rows are recorded by the parent agent by hand.

## How rounds work

1. **Check the machine first.** `curl -s
   https://qwenpaw-keepalive.qwenpaw-rohan.workers.dev/status` — if
   `status` is `waking` / `cooldown` / `conflict`, the Free machine is
   paused or cooling down: machine tests are BLOCKED that round, not
   failed. Wait and re-run.
2. **Run the protocol suite:** `python3 run-tests.py` (full) or
   `python3 run-tests.py --only T01,T02` / `--area desktop` (part).
   The runner appends the round below automatically. `--no-record`
   runs without recording (smoke runs only).
3. **Run the browser tests** (T50–T57) in a real logged-in browser
   (parent agent) and the needs-token tests (T58–T61) with the
   user-held secrets, then paste their rows into the round's table.
4. **Fix failures, re-test.** A round passes only when every protocol
   test is PASS (or KNOWN-GAP where the catalogue expects it) and the
   browser/needs-token rows for that round are filled. No "done" claim
   without a passing round (PLAN.md Phase 1).
5. **Never edit an old round.** New information goes in a new round.

## Result vocabulary

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PASS` | Check ran, expected result observed. |
| `FAIL` | Check ran, expected result NOT observed. Fix the system, not the test — unless the test itself is wrong, in which case fix TESTS.md + the runner and say so in the round notes. |

# QwenPaw test project (README.md)

A bigger test suite that exercises every QwenPaw feature built in
Phase 0 — console, desktop (Team :1 + Private :2), bridge + Camoufox,
computer-use MCP, routines, group chat, ticket board, bot pages, skills,
mailbox, heartbeat, approvals, fleet, evals, import/export, teach,
needs-you, terminal, maintenance, keep-alive + Pages proxy.

- **`TESTS.md`** — the full catalogue: 61 tests, each with id, area,
  exact check command(s), expected result, method, and evidence.
- **`run-tests.py`** — runs the 49 protocol tests, skips the rest with
  a clear mark, prints PASS/FAIL/KNOWN-GAP/NEEDS-VERIFICATION/
  NEEDS-BROWSER/NEEDS-TOKEN per test, and appends a round record to
  `RESULTS.md`.
- **`RESULTS.md`** — round records (Round 1 is the coordinator's hand-run protocol sweep; Round 2+ are `run-tests.py` runs).

JEV and Drex are NOT implemented yet — there are no tests for them
(PLAN.md Phase 2/3). The log-check option (PLAN.md Phase 1) is a
separate build, not part of this suite.

## How to run

From the repo root (`~/workspace/qwenpaw-deploy`):

```bash
# Full protocol round (records Round N in RESULTS.md)
python3 features/test-project/run-tests.py

python3 features/test-project/run-tests.py --only T01,T02,T03
python3 features/test-project/run-tests.py --area desktop
python3 features/test-project/run-tests.py --area desktop --area mcp

# Smoke run — no record appended
python3 features/test-project/run-tests.py --only T03 --no-record

# Catalogue
python3 features/test-project/run-tests.py --list
```

Exit code is 0 when no protocol test FAILs, 1 otherwise (skips and
KNOWN-GAP do not fail the run). A full round takes roughly 3–5 minutes
(Round 2 took 142 s; most of it is on-machine exec calls and the
screenshot compare).

## Runner notes (fixes landed in Round 2)

- **HTTP transport is curl, not urllib.** Python urllib raises
  `IncompleteRead` / `RemoteDisconnected` on these Cloudflare responses
  in this environment (9/9 urllib fetches failed while curl got the full

  with no length at all; curl tolerates both. `http_get` /
  `http_post_json` shell out to `curl -s -w '\n__HTTP_CODE__:%{http_code}'`
  (3 attempts, 5 s sleep, HTTP error codes never retried). Do not switch
  the runner back to urllib.

# Skill scanning — a CI gate for third-party `SKILL.md` bundles

**Status: code complete, offline, deterministic.** Run it before installing a
skill; that is the whole point. Since 2026-11-18 (gap #10) it also
enforces the skill-package schema: every `SKILL.md` carries YAML
frontmatter (name, description, when-to-use, allowed tools), only the
index built from that frontmatter is loaded by default, and a skill
body that invokes a tool outside its declared scope is flagged. See
"Frontmatter", "Tool-scope enforcement", "The index", "Self-written
skills", and "Converting the existing skills" below.

## Why a skill is not a document

QwenPaw loads a skill's `SKILL.md` into the agent's instructions, and its
scripts run with the container's authority. So a skill is **executable
policy**. One that says "when you see X, run this" is a prompt-injection
payload with a friendly filename.

The cited base rate for a public skill marketplace is brutal: NVIDIA's scan of
31,132 skills found **26.1% with vulnerabilities and 5.2% likely malicious**
(`features/research/trending-repos-2026-11-15.md` §3). Whether or not that

# Cloudflare Code Mode — Phase 5 pilot (VM runner)

A **small, bounded pilot** that measures whether Code Mode is worth adopting
for predictable jobs. It does not touch QwenPaw's loop, and it does not claim
any saving it has not measured.

Research note: `features/research/code-mode.md`.

---

## The Cloudflare path is dead. Do not retry it.

**`worker_loaders` (Dynamic Workers) requires a PAID Cloudflare plan.**

Verified live on 2026-11-16: the Cloudflare Workers API returns

```
403   code 10195   (worker_loaders is not available on this plan)
```

The account is on the free tier and the user has ruled out paying. So:

- the `[[worker_loaders]]` binding in `worker/wrangler.toml` was enabled in
  commit `8e1bdb9` **precisely to settle this question** — a commented-out
  binding cannot answer it — and the deploy attempt returned 10195;
- **`worker/wrangler.toml` and `worker/src/index.js` are kept as the record of
  what was tried**, not as something to deploy. `worker/` is now a museum
  piece with a README note, and nothing should be pointed at it;
- this will not be retried. Re-running it on a free plan cannot produce a
  different answer, and a paid plan is out of scope.

The honest cost of that: the pilot's original home is gone, and the benchmark
below survives because it never needed a loader in the first place.

---

## The replacement: run it on the VM

Execution now happens on the InstaBox machine that already runs QwenPaw —
where the MCP proxy already lives, and where a real process can actually be
bounded.

```
features/codemode/
  vm/
    codemode-runner.py      the runner: fixed job, sandbox wiring (T139),
                            HTTP surface, audit trail
    mcp.py                  MCP client: SSE discovery + JSON-RPC over POST
    test_mcp.py             27 checks against a REAL SSE + JSON-RPC server
    test_e2e.py             44 checks: runner -> real MCP -> real HTTP
  qwenpaw-codemode.service  systemd unit (Unix socket, RuntimeDirectory)
  harness-codemode.mjs      68 checks for the retired Worker (kept: it still
                            documents the measurement and its arithmetic)
  worker/                   RETIRED. Cloudflare path, kept as the record.
```

### Why the VM is a better home than the edge

| | Cloudflare Worker Loader | VM runner |
|---|---|---|
| Availability | **paid plan only** (403 / 10195) | already running |
| Bound the work | platform sandbox, opaque limits | real `RLIMIT`, wall clock, per-call timeout |
| Reach the MCP proxy | a hop from the edge into a published port | local (`172.18.0.1:8898`) |
| Cost per run | request-metered | nothing metered |
| Debug a failure | logs you cannot attach to | a process you can strace |

### The safety model, given this runs on the box holding `auth.json`

1. **Fixed job only, on main.** There is no `eval`, no `exec`, no template
   accepting caller text for the main-container job. The only way to
   change what runs there is to edit the file and commit it. An AST
   assertion in the selftest enforces the absence — a substring check
   would have passed the retired Worker's fake MCP shape.
1b. **Generated code only in the sandbox (T139).** A generated-code job
   is routed by `dispatch.route_job` and runs as uid 10001 on the
   isolated bridge `qwenpaw-sandbox-net` with a workspace-only mount,
   no docker.sock, no route to the vault broker, and a 300 s hard
   deadline. Its only credential is a 90 s scoped token on a tmpfs
   file — never the broker token, never in env. Anything that cannot
   run in the sandbox is refused with a named reason, never silently
   fallen back to main. The AST assertion now allows `subprocess`
   only via `run()`, only from the sandbox runner and its docker-kill
   helper: that is the one process the runner spawns, `docker run`.
2. **No unbounded network.** The runner talks to exactly one URL, from config,
   never from the job.
3. **Bounded time.** `JOB_DEADLINE_S = 120`, `MCP_TIMEOUT_S = 15` per call.

# D1 schema — qwenpaw-state

Database: `qwenpaw-state`, uuid `5f58a2f8-e4bb-45e5-8a94-4fc283b90871`
(created 2026-11-15 via the D1 API; read replication DISABLED, so reads
are strongly consistent). One database for all three Workers. Free-tier
headroom after migration: ~4,700 rows written/day (4.7% of 100,000),
~45,000 rows read/day (0.9% of 5,000,000), < 10 MB stored (2% of 500 MB).
See QUOTA-BUDGET.md for the full audit.

## Design choice: KV-shaped store over typed tables

The three Workers already speak KV (`get` / `put` / `delete` /
`list({prefix})`). The store module (`store.js`, inlined into each
worker — Pages `_worker.js` and the API-uploaded standalone workers are
single files with no bundler, so a shared import is not possible)
exposes the SAME interface, backed by the typed tables below. Call
sites change only the binding source (`env.DESKTOP_KV` /
`env.STATUS` -> `store(env)`); no handler logic changes. The typed
tables make the atomic operations possible later (see "Follow-ups");
the cutover itself keeps behaviour identical.

`USE_D1` env var (`"1"` = D1, anything else / unset = KV) selects the
backend at runtime. KV stays as the fallback until D1 is verified live.

## Tables

```sql
-- One row per computer. expires_at is epoch ms; the worker checks it
-- (D1 has no TTL — expiry is enforced in SQL / in the reader).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leases (
  computer   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- 'default' | 'qa'
  lease_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  holder     TEXT NOT NULL,      -- 'user'
  granted_at INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- epoch ms
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- epoch ms
  fence      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS generations (
  computer TEXT PRIMARY KEY,     -- 'default' | 'qa'
  gen      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

-- One row per computer (the old global "needsyou" key is copied to
-- computer='default' by the migration; the worker also falls back to
-- the legacy key on reads until the copy lands).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS needs_you (
  computer TEXT PRIMARY KEY,     -- 'default' | 'qa'
  text     TEXT NOT NULL,
  at       TEXT NOT NULL,        -- ISO timestamp
  run_id   TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS teach_skills (
  id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- 'taught-<random8>'
  payload    TEXT NOT NULL,      -- JSON: {id, name, goal, playbook, events, at}
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS modes (
  agent TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- agent name, sanitised
  mode  TEXT NOT NULL            -- 'team' | 'private'
);

-- Previews: ONE row per computer, upsert replaces the image (no
-- history to prune). Stored as RAW BYTES (BLOB), not base64: the
-- worker still speaks base64 to its callers, and the store
-- decodes/encodes at the boundary. No index on the BLOB.
-- Decision (evidence): live previews are 500,476 B (:1) and 707,262 B
-- (:2) (measured on the machine 2026-11-15). D1's max row/BLOB is
-- 2 MB (official docs), so a raw 707 KB preview fits with 2.8x
-- headroom; the worker caps uploads at 1,500,000 B, so a row can never
-- exceed 1.5 MB. R2 was considered and REJECTED for previews: R2 is
-- not enabled on this account (API error 10042 — enabling it is a
-- separate user step, possibly billing-gated), and it would add a
-- second store for a value that fits in D1. If previews ever exceed
-- the cap, R2 is the documented fallback.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS previews (
  computer   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- 'default' | 'qa'
  png        BLOB NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- Routine run history: one row per tick (not one JSON blob). Bounded
-- to 50 rows by the writer (DELETE oldest beyond 50). `at` is ISO.
-- `raw` holds the full entry JSON so `get` reconstructs the array
-- losslessly (entries carry extra fields like `cron`).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS routines_history (
  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  at              TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind            TEXT NOT NULL,  -- 'wake-tick' | 'daily-summary-slot' | 'manual-trigger'
  qwenpaw

# Quota budget — QwenPaw Cloudflare storage (Free tier)

Written 2026-11-15 after the KV burn of 2026-11-15 (lease-watcher
unconditional preview uploads, ~11,500 writes/day, spent the whole
account's 1,000/day KV budget by mid-morning and broke every write path
at once while reads kept working). All numbers below are computed from
the actual source in this repo, not estimated from dashboards.

## Governing free limits (Cloudflare, verified 2026-11-15)

| Limit | Free value | Scope | Resets |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV writes (put + delete) | 1,000 / day | **per account, all namespaces combined** | 00:00 UTC |
| KV reads | 100,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| KV value size | 25 MB | per key | — |
| KV, one write per key | 1 / second | per key | — |
| Workers requests | 100,000 / day | per account (Pages Functions count) | 00:00 UTC |
| Workers CPU | 10 ms / invocation | per invocation | — |
| D1 rows written | 100,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| D1 rows read | 5,000,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| D1 max row / string / BLOB | 2 MB | per row | — |
| D1 storage | 500 MB / DB, 5 GB / account | per DB / account | — |
| D1 queries / invocation | 50 (Free) | per Worker invocation | — |
| Durable Objects requests | 100,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| DO KV-backend value | 128 KiB | per value | — |
| DO SQLite-backend key+value | 8 MB combined | per key | — |

The KV write limit is the binding constraint: it is **shared across
every namespace** (STATUS + DESKTOP_KV + groupchat/board KV use), so a
burn in one worker breaks all of them at once. D1's 100,000 rows/day is
100x larger and is the reason for the migration (see SCHEMA.md).

## KV write paths — worst case per day (hard use)

"Hard use" = one user, control held 24 h, screen changing constantly,
machine waking every 5 min, routines firing on every cron, teach /
needs-you bursts. A dash means the path did not exist or was not the
burn source at that time.

| # | Path | Trigger | Current worst/day | Optimized (KV) worst/day | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | keep-alive status put | cron */5 min | 288 | **~1–10** | Write only on state change (status / lastUpAt / consecutiveFailures). A steady "up" day writes ~1. |
| K2 | keep-alive /ping, /status?live=1, /wake | manual | unbounded (1/req) | **~10–50** | Same change-only rule; manual use is rare. |
| K3 | keep-alive API-wake marker | offline/waking + key set | 144 (10-min gap) | **144** | Key currently UNSET, so 0 today. Only when a wake actually fires. |
| K4 | routines history put | cron 49/day | 49 | **~1–5** | Append only when the entry differs from the last (kind/status/httpStatus/activeRoutines). Identical ticks collapse. |
| K5 | routines /trigger | manual, 1/min rate limit | 4,320 (3 puts x 1,440) | **300** | 3 puts per trigger; new soft cap 100 triggers/day (approximate — see guard note). |

# Quota budget — QwenPaw Cloudflare storage (Free tier)

Written 2026-11-15 after the KV burn of 2026-11-15 (lease-watcher
unconditional preview uploads, ~11,500 writes/day, spent the whole
account's 1,000/day KV budget by mid-morning and broke every write path
at once while reads kept working). All numbers below are computed from
the actual source in this repo, not estimated from dashboards.

## Governing free limits (Cloudflare, verified 2026-11-15)

| Limit | Free value | Scope | Resets |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV writes (put + delete) | 1,000 / day | **per account, all namespaces combined** | 00:00 UTC |
| KV reads | 100,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| KV value size | 25 MB | per key | — |
| KV, one write per key | 1 / second | per key | — |
| Workers requests | 100,000 / day | per account (Pages Functions count) | 00:00 UTC |
| Workers CPU | 10 ms / invocation | per invocation | — |
| D1 rows written | 100,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| D1 rows read | 5,000,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| D1 max row / string / BLOB | 2 MB | per row | — |
| D1 storage | 500 MB / DB, 5 GB / account | per DB / account | — |
| D1 queries / invocation | 50 (Free) | per Worker invocation | — |
| Durable Objects requests | 100,000 / day | per account | 00:00 UTC |
| DO KV-backend value | 128 KiB | per value | — |
| DO SQLite-backend key+value | 8 MB combined | per key | — |

# Storage — off KV, onto D1

The Cloudflare KV free tier allows **1,000 writes/day per account**
(shared across all namespaces). The lease-watcher's unconditional
preview uploads burned that budget by mid-morning on 2026-11-15,
which broke every write path at once (takeover, mode, needs-you all
answered 500 while reads kept working). This directory is the fix.

## Files

- `QUOTA-BUDGET.md` — the audit: every write path, worst-case
  writes/day under hard use, the governing free limit, and headroom
  (KV phase and D1 phase, both verified live).
- `SCHEMA.md` — the D1 schema (`qwenpaw-state`,
  `5f58a2f8-e4bb-45e5-8a94-4fc283b90871`), the key -> table routing,
  and the decisions (previews as raw BLOBs, R2 rejected, board
  follow-up, atomic lease ops follow-up).
- `store.js` — the KV-shaped store over D1. `createStore(env, kv)`
  returns `{ get, put, delete, list }` with the same signatures the
  Workers already use, so call sites change only the binding source.
  D1 when `USE_D1 === "1"` and `env.QWENPAW_DB` is bound, otherwise
  the KV namespace (fallback). Inlined into each worker (Pages
  `_worker.js` and the API-uploaded standalone Workers are single
  files with no bundler — keep the copies in sync with this file).
- `harness-store.mjs` — 38 tests for the store against a mock D1
  backed by real SQLite (`node:sqlite`). Run:
  `node features/storage/harness-store.mjs` (38/38).
- `migrate-kv-to-d1.py` — the migration: access check, create/reuse
  the DB, create the tables, export KV -> import D1, attach the D1
  binding + `USE_D1=1` to both Pages projects, deploy, verify,
  rollback (flip the flag back; KV data is never deleted).
- `kv-export-2026-11-15.json` — the KV snapshot exported at migration
  time (8 keys; no secrets in it — status, definitions, history,
  generations, mode, last-wake timestamps only).

## Live state (2026-11-15)

- D1 database `qwenpaw-state` created, 12 tables, data imported
  (generations 19/2, mode private, status, 29 history rows,
  2 definitions, 0 leases, 0 previews at import time).
- All three Workers deployed with the D1 store + `USE_D1=1`:
  Pages qwenpawx `50600362` + frontend `572c5932`; keep-alive and
  routines via `cf.py put-worker` with the D1 metadata.
- Verified: Pages reads generations from D1; previews land in D1 as
  raw BLOBs (500,429 B / 707,640 B); routines reads definitions from
  D1; keep-alive returns fresh probes and skips the write on a steady
  "up" day (change-only working as designed).
- KV budget is spent for 2026-11-15 UTC (error 10048) — nothing
  writes to KV now. D1 restores write functionality immediately.

## Rollback

Set `USE_D1=0` (Pages: PATCH the env var on both projects;
Workers: redeploy with the metadata without the `USE_D1` var) and
redeploy. KV data was never deleted. Leases expire within 90 s, so
a stale KV lease is harmless; the only durable loss on a flip-back
is teach skills / routine definitions / history written to D1 after
the cutover — see `migrate-kv-to-d1.py rollback`.

# #9 — Spaces / Access

Status: **Partial (design only — NOT enforced).** Nothing in this item
changes who can reach QwenPaw today. It prepares the design so enforcement
is a small, reviewed step once the prerequisites exist.

## What was checked live (2026-11-15)

1. **Cloudflare account has zero zones** (`GET /client/v4/zones` → `[]`).
   Cloudflare Access (Zero Trust) policies attach to applications on a
   zone or a custom domain. The console is reached via
   `qwenpawx.pages.dev` (Cloudflare's zone, not the user's) and the raw
   InstaBox URL — neither can take an Access policy from this account.
   Enforcement is impossible until a custom domain exists.
2. **QwenPaw has single-user auth, no per-user RBAC.** Verified:
   `POST /api/auth/login` takes one username/password; the account is
   `satwik`. There is a channel-level allow-list mechanism
   (`allow_from`, `access_control_dm/group` per channel in `agent.json`),
   and an `access_control.py` router, but no concept of "person A sees
   space X, person B sees space Y".
3. **Multi-agent exists, multi-person does not.** `config.json` has two
   agent profiles (`default`, `QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2`), both enabled.
   Workspaces are per-agent, not per-person.

## What is built

### 1. Access policy design (draft only)

`access-policy-draft.json` — a Cloudflare Access application + policy
draft for the future custom domain. **Not applied.** Design:

- Application: the console on the custom domain (e.g.
  `qwenpaw.<user-domain>`), covering the Pages proxy.
- Policy 1 (allow): the user's email (the one the user will confirm),
  session 24 h, no service token.
- Policy 2 (deny): everyone else.
- Explicitly **not** included: device posture checks, Warp requirement,
  or Service Auth — too easy to lock the user out.
- Rule (hard): never enable enforcement without the user testing the
  login path first on a separate application (e.g. the `/status` page),
  and never apply it to the raw InstaBox URL (Access cannot cover it).

### 2. Per-space workspace mapping (draft)

A "space" here means one agent workspace with its own prompts, memory,
and channels. Mapping today:

| Space | Workspace | Who | Status |
|-------|-----------|-----|--------|
| Personal | `default` | Rohan | Live |
| QA / setup help | `QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2` | Rohan | Live |
| Research | `research-assistant` (template) | Rohan | Template only, not installed |
| Household | `household-manager` (template) | Rohan | Template only, not installed |
| Code | `code-helper` (template) | Rohan | Template only, not installed |

All spaces belong to one person. That is the honest scope of "spaces" in
QwenPaw: **one user, many agents**. True per-person spaces (family
members, teammates, each with private memory) need a different app —
QwenPaw cannot do it, and no Access policy can add it: Access controls
who reaches the front door, not what they see inside.

## What is blocked, exactly

1. **Custom domain on Cloudflare** (user-owned domain added as a zone,
   free) + Pages custom domain pointing at `qwenpawx.pages.dev`.
   Until then, no Access application can exist.
2. **User's email address** for the allow policy (to be confirmed by the
   user — not guessed).
3. **A tested login path**: apply Access to a throwaway path first, log in
   as the user, then move it to the console. Never enforce blind.
4. **Per-person spaces**: needs a different application. Do not promise it.

## What NOT to do

- Do not enable Cloudflare Access on any URL the user currently uses
  without a tested rollback (removing the policy). Lockout risk is real
  and this build does not take it.
- Do not use the raw InstaBox URL as the "private" path: it is public,
  and QwenPaw auth is the only gate there.

Status: **Done (read + dry-run only).** `features/infra/scripts/fleet.py` lists the real
fleet from the live config. Enable/schedule are **dry-run only by design**.

## Verified config keys (read live 2026-11-15, QwenPaw v2.3.0)

`working/config.json`, section `agents`:

| Key | Value observed | Meaning |
|-----|---------------|---------|
| `agents.active_agent` | `"default"` | Agent the console opens on |
| `agents.agent_order` | `["default"]` | Display order (note: QA agent is **not** in this list even though its profile exists) |
| `agents.profiles.<id>` | `{id, workspace_dir, enabled, pinned}` | Per-agent registration |
| `agents.profiles.default.enabled` | `true` | |
| `agents.profiles.QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2.enabled` | `true` | |
| `agents.defaults.heartbeat` | `{enabled: false, every: "6h", target: "main", timeoutSeconds: 300}` | **Global**, not per-agent |
| `agents.running.max_iters` | `100` | Loop guard |

Per workspace, `workspaces/<id>/agent.json`:

| Key | Example |
|-----|---------|
| `id` / `name` / `description` | `default` / `Default` / `default agent`; QA: `QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2` / `QA Agent` / `Builtin Q&A helper…` |
| `workspace_dir` | `/app/working/workspaces/default` (container path) |
| `backend` / `backend_settings` | `qwenpaw` / `{}` |
| `template_id` | only on QA (`"qa"`) |
| `channels.<name>.enabled` | per-channel flags; only `console` is `true` on both agents |

Global model (not per-agent): `working.secret/providers/active_model.json`
→ `xingchiapi/gpt-6-astra` (verified live by `fleet.py` 2026-11-15; the
user switched the default chat model from Kilo to GPT Astra during this
build). Fleet shows it as the shared model; per-agent
models do not exist in this version (the Rakazo gap note about
"per-agent models" being partial refers to session-level overrides, not
fleet config — not verified here, not claimed).

## What the script does

```
# on the machine (config.json is root-owned, so sudo):
sudo python3 features/infra/scripts/fleet.py list
sudo python3 features/infra/scripts/fleet.py show QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2
sudo python3 features/infra/scripts/fleet.py enable --dry-run <agent-id>
sudo python3 features/infra/scripts/fleet.py schedule --dry-run <agent-id> [--every 6h]
```

- `list`: active agent, agent order, active model, heartbeat defaults,
  and one row per agent (enabled, active, name, channels on).
- `show`: full JSON for one agent.
- `enable --dry-run`: prints the exact `config.json` change that *would*
  be made (`agents.profiles.<id>.enabled: true`) and stops. It never
  writes.
- `schedule --dry-run`: prints the heartbeat change that *would* be made
  and warns that heartbeat is global in v2.3.0 — per-agent targeting via
  `target` is **not verified** (`target` defaults to `"main"`).

## Why dry-run only

1. `config.json` must never be edited by a script without approval (task
   hard rule).
2. Enabling an agent almost certainly needs a container restart: the
   multi-agent manager preloads agents at startup (log: `Agent startup
   complete: 2/2 agents started successfully`). The restart requirement
   is **unverified** — the script says so instead of assuming.
3. A bad edit to `config.json` breaks the whole console. The script
   refuses to be the thing that does that.

## What still needs the coordinator/user

- To actually enable/disable an agent or change the heartbeat: approve
  the exact JSON diff, edit `config.json`, restart the container, and
  verify both agents still preload (`docker logs` / log tail).
- To add a new agent to the fleet: import a template (see
  `19-import-export.md`), register it in `agents.profiles` (+
  `agent_order`), restart, verify.

# #14 — Credentials vault

Status: **Partial (approximation).** There is no protected-card flow in
QwenPaw, and this build does not pretend otherwise. What is built is the
best approximation the platform allows: secrets stay in `working.secret`,
a server-side-only read convention for skills, and a names-only inventory.

## The honest limit

Rakazo-style vaults show a secret as a protected card the agent can use
without the user (or the chat) ever seeing the value. QwenPaw v2.3.0 has
no such mechanism:

- Provider credentials are JSON files under `working.secret/providers/`.
- There is no per-secret access policy, no scoped token, no UI that
  redacts a value while letting a skill use it.
- Any skill code running on the machine can read any file the container
  can read. That is the trust boundary: **the machine is the vault**.
- The `.master_key` file in `working.secret/` is QwenPaw's encryption key
  for credentials it stores encrypted (e.g. mailbox `auth_code`). Name
  only — never copy, share, or print it.

## What is built

### 1. Inventory — `vault-inventory.md` (names only, verified live)

Every secret's **name and location, never its value**. Verified
2026-11-15 by listing directories only.

### 2. Server-side-only read convention (for skills)

This is a rule, not a feature — but it is the rule that keeps secrets out
of chat:

1. A skill that needs a credential reads it **from the file** at run time
   (e.g. `working.secret/providers/custom/xingchiapi.json`), inside the
   container, in code — never by asking the user to paste it into chat,
   and never by echoing it into a reply, a log, or a tool result.
2. The credential value must never appear in: chat text, tool-call
   arguments shown to the user, `qwenpaw.log`, `agent.json`, `config.json`,
   git, or any file under `working/` (as opposed to `working.secret/`).
3. Only the **name** of a credential may be mentioned to the user
   ("using the Kilo key"), never the value, a prefix, or a length.
4. If a skill needs a credential that does not exist yet, it asks the user
   to add it in Console → Settings → Models/Providers (the console writes
   it to `working.secret/`). It does not ask for the value in chat.
5. Rotation: edit/replace the file on the machine (coordinator step),
   then restart the container for the provider manager to pick it up
   (restart requirement assumed, not verified — provider restore runs at
   startup per the log line `Background local model restore completed`).

### 3. What already follows this convention

- The mailbox skill: `agent.json` holds only public mailbox config;
  `auth_code`/`password`/`phone_number` are absent from `agent.json` and
  redacted from API responses; the encrypted credential is resolved into
  a DriverCard only at runtime (per the skill's own SKILL.md).
- LLM provider keys: kept as separate files under
  `working.secret/providers/`; `config.json` `providers` is empty by
  design (verified: `providers` key is absent/`None` in `config.json`).

## What is NOT built (and why)

- No encryption UI, no secret rotation automation, no per-skill scoping.
  All three need changes inside QwenPaw itself (or a sidecar vault
  service, which InstaBox Free cannot run alongside QwenPaw on 1 machine
  without risking the 8 GB RAM budget).
- No backup of `working.secret/` into git or Cloudflare — that would be a
  leak, not a feature. `working.secret/` is covered by machine snapshots
  (`qwenpaw-ready`, `qwenpaw-before-rakazo-build`) and by
  `scripts/backup.sh`; verify snapshot coverage with the coordinator.

# #22 — Evals / prompt versioning

Status: **Done (runner built, live run pending creds).** Prompts are
versioned; the runner is written and dry-run verified. It has **not** been
run live — no credentials were read or stored during this build, and the
first live run needs the user/coordinator to supply them.

## Prompt versioning — done

`prompts/v1/` holds exact copies of the live default agent's prompts,
snapshotted 2026-11-15 (byte counts match the live files: SOUL 1,679,
PROFILE 726, AGENTS 1,870, HEARTBEAT 171). Rules in `prompts/v1/README.md`:
new versions go in a new directory (`v2/`), never by overwriting `v1/`;
prompts only, never MEMORY/chats/history.

## Eval runner — built, live run pending

`evals/run-evals.py` + `evals/cases.json` (5 fixed cases: identity in
English, English-only answer, no-China-endpoint answer, timezone
awareness, destructive-action refusal).

Verified API surface (read from the installed QwenPaw v2.3.0 source):

- `POST /api/auth/login` `{"username","password"}` → `{"token","username"}`
- `POST /api/console/chat/task` with Agent API envelope
  `{"channel":"console","user_id":"eval","session_id":"eval-<case>",`
  `"input":[{"content":[{"type":"text","text": <prompt>"}]}],"timeout": N}`
  → `{"task_id": ...}`
- `GET /api/console/chat/task/{task_id}` → task status
- Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (verified in `auth.py`)
- Login is rate-limited: 423 = locked, 429 = throttled with `Retry-After`

Runner behaviour (per source + GPT Astra design review):

- Logs in **once** per run, token in memory only, never written to disk.
- 423 ends the run immediately; 429 honours `Retry-After` + backoff.
- 401 on a task call: one re-login, retry once.
- Pass/fail is a case-insensitive substring check on the reply; every run
  writes one JSONL file with the raw task response, so a failure can be
  inspected by hand. If the task response shape is not recognised, the
  case is marked **unverified**, never faked as pass.
- `--dry-run` validates the cases and prints the exact request envelope
  with no login and no network calls. Dry-run was verified locally.

## What still needs the user/coordinator

1. Run the first live eval: `QWENPAW_USER=satwik QWENPAW_PASS='...' python3
   evals/run-evals.py` (from the machine, or anywhere that can reach the
   console URL). The password must be supplied at run time, never stored.
   Note: the default chat model changed during this build from Kilo to
   GPT Astra (`xingchiapi/gpt-6-astra`, user action 01:04 IST) — evals
   will run against Astra unless the model is changed back first.
2. Review the recorded replies: substring checks are heuristic. The
   `destructive-refusal` case especially needs a human read.
3. After any prompt change (new `prompts/v2/`), re-run and keep the
   results file next to the new version.

## Limits (honest)

- No GPU/benchmark harness, no LLM judge — substring checks only.
- The `GET /chat/task/{id}` response shape was read from the router
  signature, not from a live response; the runner handles unknown shapes
  by marking cases unverified. If the first live run shows a different
  shape, the extractor in `run-evals.py` needs one update, not a redesign.
- Evals run against the live agent, so they create real eval chats in the
  console (session ids `eval-<case>`). That is by design and visible.

   greeting "Hi! This is QwenPaw. How can I help you?".
   `channels.sip` (`enabled: false`): `sip_mode "dev"`, `sip_port 5061`,
   `livekit_url ""`, `livekit_api_key ""`, `livekit_api_secret ""`,
   `livekit_sip_trunk_id ""`; TTS google, STT deepgram.
2. **Voice ingress exists in code but has no service behind it.**
   `/voice/incoming` (TwiML-style), `/voice/ws`, `/voice/status-callback`
   delegate to a `channel_ingress` plugin service; with no service the
   endpoint returns 503 / "Voice channel is not available."

4. Run `features/infra/scripts/voice-readiness.py` on the machine any time to re-check
   which fields are set (names only, never values).

## Paths, and exactly what each needs

### A. Twilio voice channel (built into QwenPaw — the direct path)

Needs from the user: a Twilio account + **Account SID**, **Auth Token**,
and a **purchased phone number**, entered in Console → Settings →
Channels → Voice, then enable the channel.

Verified pricing (Twilio US price list, Oct 2026; third-party summaries
agree): $15 trial credit for new accounts; US local number $1.15/mo;
receive $0.0085/min, place $0.0140/min (US). Trial accounts can call only
verified numbers and expire after 30 days per Twilio docs summaries.
For India: outbound to Indian mobiles $0.0496/min, landlines $0.0699/min
(Sept 2026); Twilio sells no Indian local/mobile numbers — only
international numbers from $1.15/mo. Confirm on Twilio's pricing page
before budgeting; prices change.

### B. SIP via LiveKit (fields already in QwenPaw's SIP channel)

Needs from the user: a LiveKit Cloud project + **LiveKit URL, API key,
API secret, SIP trunk ID**, entered in the SIP channel settings, plus a
phone number on a SIP trunk.

Verified pricing (LiveKit pricing page via third-party summaries, Oct–Nov
2026): **Build plan is free** — 1,000 agent session minutes/mo, 5
concurrent sessions, **1 free US local number, 50 US local inbound
minutes/mo**, 1,000 third-party SIP minutes; Build is a hard cap (requests
fail when it runs out, nothing is billed). Ship is $50/mo. This is the
cheapest real path to a working phone line — but it is **not built or
tested here**: the QwenPaw↔LiveKit bridge (LiveKit room → QwenPaw agent)
is not part of this build and its wiring is unverified. Expect a build +
test step with the coordinator before it can take a call.

### C. ElevenLabs agent (separate product, not QwenPaw)

No integration in QwenPaw. An ElevenLabs conversational agent with a
phone number is a separate agent, not this QwenPaw, and needs an
ElevenLabs account + phone number (paid). It would not share QwenPaw's
memory, workspace, or tools. Only choose this if the user wants a
standalone voice agent instead of QwenPaw on the phone.

QwenPaw voice bridge — same missing pieces as path B, with no phone
number at the end. Not built.

  Every credential field above is empty today.
- No live test call has been made (there is no number to call).

## What is built

### `features/infra/scripts/workspace-export.py`

Usage (run on the machine via `ib.py exec`, or anywhere with a workspace
copy):

```
python3 workspace-export.py export <workspace-dir> <out.tgz>
python3 workspace-export.py import <archive.tgz> <dest-workspace-dir> [--backup-dir DIR]
python3 workspace-export.py verify <archive.tgz>
```

- **Export allowlist only** (identity + prompts + skills, no history):
  top-level `agent.json`, `SOUL.md`, `PROFILE.md`, `MEMORY.md`,
  `AGENTS.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `CONTACTS.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`,
  `MAIL_TRIAGE.md`, `skill.json`, `jobs.json`, and the `skills/` directory.
- **Always excluded**: `history.db*`, `sessions/`, `checkpoints/`,
  `state/`, `memory/`, `mem_agent/`, `mem_session/`, `mem_metadata/`,
  `media/`, `resource/`, `drivers/`, `digest/`, `*.shm`, `*.wal`.
  Export never carries chats, sessions, or credentials.
- Safety checks: source must contain `agent.json` + `SOUL.md`; the
  tarball carries a `manifest.json` (agent id, exported_at, per-file
  sha256); import verifies every hash, refuses path traversal in tar
  members, refuses to overwrite an existing workspace unless
  `--backup-dir` is given (existing dir is moved aside first, never
  deleted).
- The script never touches the live workspace unless you point it at one.
  The documented test flow exports a **copy**.

### Test evidence (2026-11-15, live machine)

- Copied `/data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2` to
  `/tmp/ws-test-src` (a copy; live workspace untouched).
- Ran export on the copy → tarball created; `verify` passed (manifest
  hashes matched).
- Ran import into `/tmp/ws-test-dst` → identity files (`agent.json`,
  `SOUL.md`, `PROFILE.md`, `AGENTS.md`) byte-identical to the copy;
  `history.db*` and `sessions/` confirmed absent from the archive.
- Live workspace checksums were not modified (no writes to
  `/data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/` at any point).

### `templates/` — starter agent templates

Three English templates, each a ready-to-import workspace folder
(`agent.json` + `SOUL.md` + `PROFILE.md` + `MEMORY.md` + `AGENTS.md`).
`workspace_dir` in each `agent.json` is a placeholder
(`/app/working/workspaces/<id>`) — set the real id on import.

| Template | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `research-assistant/` | Web research + summarising, cites sources, never invents citations |
| `household-manager/` | Routines, reminders, shopping lists, home admin for Rohan |
| `code-helper/` | Code review + small fixes, tests before claiming done, no destructive commands |

Import a template with:
`python3 features/infra/scripts/workspace-export.py import` — no: templates are plain
folders, copy one to `/data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/<new-id>/`
on the machine (coordinator step — creating a workspace is a write to the
live tree, so it is not done by this build), then restart is required for
QwenPaw to preload it (restart needs user approval; not done here).
New workspaces are **not** auto-discovered without a restart — the
multi-agent manager preloads agents at startup (verified in the log:
`Agent startup complete: 2/2 agents started`).

## Limits (honest)

- Export is identity/prompts/skills only. Chat history, sessions, memory
  stores (`mem_*`, `memory/`), checkpoints and media are deliberately
  **not** portable by this tool. Full backup remains `scripts/backup.sh`
  / snapshots.
- Import does not register the agent in `config.json`
  (`agents.profiles` / `agent_order`) — that file must never be edited by
  a script without approval, and the agent must be picked up at startup.
  Registration is a coordinator step, documented in `11-fleet-manager.md`.

# #1 — Live computer alternative

Status: **Blocked (no remote desktop) / Done (activity feed).** The honest
finding is that no live-desktop path exists on this machine — and the
activity feed that replaces it is deployed and verified live.

## What was checked live (2026-11-15)

### The desktop exists, but it cannot be seen or controlled remotely

- `Xvfb :1 -screen 0 1280x800x24` is running, with a full XFCE session
  (`xfce4-session`, panel, notification daemon) since boot.
- **No VNC server process is running.** `tigervncserver` is installed,
  but no `Xvnc`/`vncserver` process exists.
- **No listening VNC/noVNC port.** `ss -tlnp` shows only port 22 (SSH)
  and `127.0.0.1:8088` (QwenPaw). No 5900, no 6080, no websockify.
- **No browser is installed** (`chromium`, `google-chrome`, `firefox`:
  none found). The 2026-11-15 cleanup removed chromium/node, which the
  cleanup note itself says degrades InstaBox's built-in
  computer-use/desktop feature.
- `novnc` / `websockify` are not installed.

Conclusion: starting a VNC server would be possible in principle
(`tigervncserver :1` exists as a binary), but it would need a listening
port exposed through InstaBox's proxy (no public port besides 8088 is
documented for this machine), a password, and a browser or viewer — and
it would consume RAM on a machine already running a 4.32 GB QwenPaw
image under an 8 GB cap. That is a new service on the user's only
machine, not a small step, and it was **not** started here: it needs the
user/coordinator to choose it explicitly. InstaBox's own built-in
computer-use streams the desktop through InstaBox's control plane, not
through a port on the machine, and that path cannot be verified from
inside the VM.

## What is built instead (verified live)

**Activity feed Worker: `qwenpaw-infra-activity`**
`https://qwenpaw-infra-activity.qwenpaw-rohan.workers.dev/`

- `GET /` — a live activity page (HTML): QwenPaw status from the STATUS
  KV namespace (written every 5 min by `qwenpaw-keepalive`), last-up time,
  consecutive failures, last check, a live-probe button, a wake button
  (via the keepalive `/wake` endpoint), and a link to take over in the
  console at `https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/`.
- `GET /api/status` — the same data as JSON.
- `GET /api/live` — probes the console URL live (no retry) and updates KV.
- The Worker reads the **same KV namespace** the keepalive uses
  (`STATUS`, `6a91d8099ed8419c88c94b0946186a27`) under its own key
  prefix; it never writes the keepalive's key, so the two cannot corrupt
  each other.
- No secrets, no chat content, no auth: it publishes status only.
  (Machine state via the InstaBox API is an optional extra — it needs an
  `INSTABOX_API_KEY` Worker Secret, which only the coordinator can set
  because the key lives in the connector store, not on the machine.)

Deploy: `workers/activity-feed/index.js` + `metadata.json`, uploaded with
`cf.py put-worker` (Cloudflare API). Verified live after deploy:
`GET /` → 200, `GET /api/status` → the keepalive KV record (`status:
"up"`, `checkedAt` within the last 5 min), `GET /api/live` → live probe
`status: "up", httpStatus: 200`. Two deploy gotchas, recorded in
`metadata.json`: (1) a top-level `vars` object is silently dropped by the
upload API — plain-text vars must be `plain_text` bindings; (2) a freshly
uploaded script has its `workers.dev` route **disabled** (requests get
Cloudflare error 1042 / 404) — enable it with `POST
/workers/scripts/qwenpaw-infra-activity/subdomain {"enabled": true}`
(`PUT` returns 10405 for API tokens; `PATCH …/settings` needs multipart
and does not take `workers_dev`).

## What the feed honestly cannot show

- It cannot show a live desktop, a screenshot, or the XFCE session.
- It cannot show what the agent is doing inside a session (no log access
  from a Worker; the log lives on the paused-or-running machine).
- "Live" means "last keepalive probe + on-demand probe", not a stream.
  During a max-run cooldown the feed correctly shows `cooldown` with

`workers/email-router/index.js` (+ `metadata.json`) — a Cloudflare Email

- Parses the incoming RFC 822 message (plain-text body; HTML parts and
  attachments are dropped in v1 and the sender is told so in the delivered
  note — attachments are never executed or stored).
- Rejects mail over 100 KB.
- Treats email content as **untrusted input**: a fixed delivery template
  wraps the sender/subject/body, and the mail can never choose the agent,
  the API path, or the session.

  `{channel: "console", user_id: "email:<sender>", session_id: "email-inbox",
  input: [{content: [{type: "text", text: <templated message>}]}], timeout: 300}`.

  caches the token in memory and in KV with a short TTL, re-logs in once on
  401, **stops immediately on 423 lockout** (never retries a lockout),
  honours `Retry-After` on 429. Credentials live only as Worker Secrets
  (`QWENPAW_USER`, `QWENPAW_PASS`) — never in KV, never in code, never
  logged.
- Replies to the sender only with a generic accept/fail note; upstream
  errors are never leaked to the sender.

---
name: github
description: "Work with GitHub through the REST API: list repositories, read files and issues, open issues and pull requests, and commit small file changes. Use whenever the user asks about a GitHub repo, an issue or PR, or wants a file read from or written to GitHub. No gh CLI is installed; this skill uses curl and python3 against api.github.com."
version: "1.0"
metadata:
  qwenpaw:
    emoji: "🐙"
    requires:
      bins: ["python3", "curl"]
      env: ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]
---

# GitHub

Work with GitHub through the REST API at `https://api.github.com`.
There is no `gh` CLI in the container, so use `curl` (or `python3`
with `urllib`) for every call.

## Authentication

- The token comes from the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable, injected
  from QwenPaw's encrypted environment store at runtime.
- **Never print, log, paste or guess the token.** If it is missing, stop
  and tell the user to set it (see "Token setup" below). Never ask the
  user to paste a token into chat.
- Every request sends:
  `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN` and
  `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and
  `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`.
- If a call returns 401, the token is missing, expired or revoked: stop
  and tell the user to check it. If it returns 403 with a rate-limit
  message, stop and report the limit instead of retrying.

## Read operations (no confirmation needed)

- List the user's repos:
  `curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" "https://api.github.com/user/repos?per_page=100"`
- Read a file: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}` (add
  `?ref={branch}` for a non-default branch). The response `content`
  field is base64; decode it, do not show the raw base64 to the user.
- List issues: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?state=open`
- Read one issue or PR: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}`
- List PRs: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open`
- Search code or issues: `GET /search/issues?q={query}` or
  `GET /search/code?q={query}` (search is rate-limited; keep queries
  narrow and paginate with `per_page`).

Default repository for this setup is `Ratulbaba7/qwenpaw-deploy`
(branch `main`). If the user names a different repo, use that one.

## Write operations (confirm with the user first)

Confirm the exact change with the user before any write, and report the
resulting URL afterwards. Writes:

- Open an issue: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues` with
  `{"title": "...", "body": "..."}`.
- Comment on an issue or PR: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments`
  with `{"body": "..."}`.
- Open a pull request: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` with
  `{"title": "...", "head": "<branch>", "base": "main", "body": "..."}`.
- Create or update a small file: `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`
  with `{"message": "...", "content": "<base64>", "branch": "main"}`.
  Updating an existing file also needs its current `sha` from a prior
  GET. Prefer small, single-file commits; for larger changes ask the user
  to make them from their own checkout instead.

Do not delete repos, force-push, or merge PRs unless the user explicitly
asks for that exact action.

## Token setup (for the user, done once)

Create a token at https://github.com/settings/tokens (classic token
with the `repo` scope, or a fine-grained token scoped to the repos the
agent may touch). Store it in QwenPaw's encrypted environment store,
never in a file or in chat:

```bash
qwenpaw env set GITHUB_TOKEN <token>
```

Run inside the QwenPaw container. The value is encrypted at rest in
`working.secret/envs.json` and is only injected into the agent's
environment at runtime. To remove it:
`qwenpaw env delete GITHUB_TOKEN`.

Until the token is set, this skill can explain GitHub concepts but cannot
call the API: say so plainly instead of pretending to have read a repo.

What QwenPaw is connected to today, how each connection works, and what
to add next — one at a time. Verified against the live machine on
2026-11-15 (`working/config.json`, skill pool, container tooling).
There is **no integration catalog** in this setup: nothing here claims
a store of ready-made app integrations exists.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `github-SKILL.md` | Source copy of the `github` skill installed on the machine. |
| `README.md` | This document. |

## New: GitHub skill (built 2026-11-15)

- Installed: `working/skill_pool/github/SKILL.md` and
  `working/workspaces/default/skills/github/SKILL.md` (identical).
- Mechanism: **skill calling a REST API** (no `gh` CLI in the
  container). `curl`/`python3` against `https://api.github.com` with
  `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Token: `GITHUB_TOKEN` from QwenPaw's encrypted env store
  (`working.secret/envs.json`, encrypted at rest). Set once by the user
  inside the container: `qwenpaw env set GITHUB_TOKEN <token>`
  (classic token with `repo` scope, or a fine-grained token scoped to
  the repos the agent may touch). Never in a file, never in chat.
  The skill declares it as `requires: {env: [GITHUB_TOKEN]}` so QwenPaw
  injects it into the skill's environment at runtime.
- Covers: list repos, read files, list/read issues and PRs, open issues,
  comment, open PRs, small single-file commits. Writes need user
  confirmation first.
- Default repo: `Ratulbaba7/qwenpaw-deploy` (branch `main`).
- **Blocked until the user sets the token.** Without it the skill says
  so plainly instead of pretending to have read a repo.

isolation). That is the right long-term upgrade (see "Next" below), but
the skill uses QwenPaw's own sanctioned secret mechanism today —

binary is available in the container right now (no Node runtime; it was
removed in the 2026-11-15 cleanup) and the REST skill works with tools
already present (`curl`, `python3`).

  `working/workspaces/default/skills/github/SKILL.md` (identical).

## #2 design — read this before using it

### Verified facts the design rests on

1. **QwenPaw already has native bot-to-bot chat.** The agent tools
   `list_agents()`, `chat_with_agent(...)`, `submit_to_agent(...)`,
   `check_agent_task(...)` and the CLI `qwenpaw agents chat` (see the
   built-in skills `chat_with_agent` and `multi_agent_collaboration`)
   send a message to another agent via `POST /api/console/chat` with
   header `X-Agent-Id: <target>` and body
   `{session_id, user_id, input: [{role: "user", content: [{type: "text",
   text: "..."}]}], request_context: {root_agent_id: <caller>}}`
   (verified in `qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py`
   `build_agent_chat_request` and `qwenpaw/cli/agents_cmd.py`).
2. **Only loopback can call that endpoint without auth.**
   `security.allow_no_auth_hosts: ["127.0.0.1", "::1"]` in
   `working/config.json`; `qwenpaw/app/auth.py` `AuthMiddleware` returns
   401 without a Bearer token otherwise. Verified live: `GET /api/agents`
   and `qwenpaw agents list` work from inside the container with no
   token; the public URL requires login.
3. **There is no native shared group thread.** Each agent-to-agent call
   is a separate 1:1 session. The Worker below supplies the shared
   thread; the relay supplies delivery.

### How a group discussion flows (automated vs manual)

```
You / user                    Worker (Durable Object thread)              Relay (on machine)
  │ POST /thread/start           │                                 │
  │ POST /thread/message         │                                 │
  │  {role:user, text}           │                                 │
  │ ───────────────────────────► │  stores message, next_agent     │
  │                              │  stays "default"                │
  │                              │ ◄── relay polls GET /thread ─── │
  │                              │     every 20 s                  │
  │                              │      delivers digest to default │
  │                              │      via `qwenpaw agents chat` │
  │                              │      (loopback, no token)       │
  │                              │      posts default's reply ───► │
  │                              │  next_agent = QA agent          │
  │                              │ ◄── relay delivers digest to QA │
  │                              │      posts QA's reply ────────► │
  │                              │  round ends, waits for user     │
  └─ GET /thread to read ────────┘
```

- **Automated once the relay runs:** user message in → both agents
  reply in turn → replies land in the shared thread. Turn order is
  enforced twice (Worker returns 409 `not_your_turn` to a wrong-agent
  post; the relay only delivers to `state.next_agent`).
- **Manual until the relay is installed:** the Worker alone only stores
  the thread. Without the relay, someone (or an agent, using the
  `delegate` skill and the native `chat_with_agent` tool) must read the
  thread and carry messages

# Smart sleep/wake, part 1: keep-alive ON/OFF toggle + max-run guard (2026-11-19)

Two additions to the intelligent sleep/wake system in `worker/src/index.js`
(see `features/sleepwake/README.md` for the base design). The §3
recovery fix was DEPLOYED LIVE 2026-11-19 ~13:20 IST (flip verified:
07:55 tick sleeping→running, reason `reporter_up`); that deploy
exposed the §4 stale-baseline defect, whose fix (§4) is code-complete
and NOT yet deployed — see §4 for the deploy condition.

## 1. Keep-alive ON/OFF toggle

### Storage
D1 `meta` table, two keys:
- `keepalive:enabled` — `'1'` (ON) | `'0'` (OFF). **Absent = ON.**
- `keepalive:updated` — ISO timestamp of the last flip.

No seed row was added, deliberately: `features/storage/schema.sql`
predates the `meta` table entirely (it has no `meta` table and no seed
for it — the live `meta` table was created via the D1 API, see
`features/storage/SCHEMA.md`), so there is no migration/seed file for
this key to live in. Absent = ON makes a seed unnecessary for the live
DB: a database that has never seen a flip behaves exactly as today.

### Endpoint: POST /keepalive
- Auth: header `Authorization: Bearer <WAKE_TOKEN>` **only** — never
  `?token=` (tokens in URLs leak in logs/Referer). The token is
  `WAKE_TOKEN`, already a Worker secret; **no new secret was invented**.
  The comparison copies the `/report` handler's length + `charCodeAt`
  loop pattern.
- Body: a JSON object with boolean `enabled` (`{"enabled": false}`).
- Success: `200 {ok: true, enabled: boolean, updatedAt: ISO}` and
  exactly **2 D1 meta writes** (`keepalive:enabled` + `keepalive:updated`).
  It does NOT sleep, wake, or probe — it only flips the toggle the next
  cron tick reads.
- Errors: `400` bad body (not JSON, not an object, or `enabled` not a
  boolean — no writes); `401` bad/missing token (no writes);
  `503` not-configured (`WAKE_TOKEN` unset) or storage failure (no D1 /
  write failed); `405` for non-POST (`GET /keepalive` -> 405 with
  `Allow: POST`).

### Tick gate (in `keepAliveTick`)
At the VERY TOP of the D1 branch — before any probe, wake, sleep, or
state write, but AFTER the no-D1 legacy-probe branch, which is
unchanged: the toggle requires D1, which is the deployed configuration
(`USE_D1=1`); a Worker without D1 keeps the old probe behaviour and the
toggle simply does not apply there.

The toggle is read with the new exported `readKeepAliveEnabled(db)`,
folded into the same D1 meta reads as the other decision inputs (0 extra
Worker requests — D1 queries are not requests). It does NOT reuse
`swMetaGet`, which swallows errors and returns null: the gate must be
able to tell "absent" (ON) from "unreadable" (HOLD). The function
returns the raw value (`null` absent, `'0'`, `'1'`, or any invalid value
as-is) and THROWS on a read error; the tick maps both error cases to
HOLD:

| Toggle value | Tick result |
|---|---|
| `'1'` or absent | Falls through to `decideSleepWake` exactly as today |
| `'0'` | `{action: 'skip', reason: 'keepalive-off'}` — no probe, no wake, no sleep, no state write |
| read throws | `{action: 'hold', reason: 'keepalive-read-error'}` — ZERO fetches, ZERO writes |
| anything else (e.g. `'yes'`) | Same HOLD as a read error |

Fail-closed throughout: an unreadable or invalid toggle never assumes
ON (which would keep waking a machine the user switched off) and never
assumes OFF (which would silently stop waking for routines).

### Status fields
- `GET /status` gains public read-only `keepAlive` (`"on" | "off" |
  "unknown"`) and `keepAliveUpdatedAt` (ISO string or null), read from D1
  in the handler — no extra client request. If D1 is unavailable the
  fields are omitted. Absent = `"on"`; unreadable or invalid = `"unknown"`.
- `GET /status` also gains `sleepwake: {nextRoutineAt, nextRoutineSource}`
  — the next scheduled run, computed with the same `computeNextRoutine`
  the cron tick uses. Fix 2026-11-19 (found in integration review): the
  stored status never carried a `sleepwake` field — the

# MCP client — stdio + streamable HTTP, per-server allowlist, namespaced tools

**Status: code complete + machine-free harness green (T128, 61/61).
NOT verified live — no machine deploy, no real MCP server, no browser
check. That half is the parent's job (Muse after sync).**

## What this is

A full MCP client for QwenPaw (gap #8 in the 2026-11-18 agent research:
MCP is the canonical extension surface in Goose, Claude Code and Codex;
skills are progressive disclosure). One real client buys hundreds of
integrations (GitHub, browser, files, calendars) without building each
one as a bespoke skill, and MCP servers are just subprocesses — it fits
a Free box.

## What already existed (not duplicated)

`features/codemode/vm/mcp.py` is a minimal **legacy SSE** client for the
machine's computer-use proxy (GET `/sse`, endpoint event, responses on
the stream). It has no allowlist, no namespacing, no stdio transport,
no streamable-HTTP transport, no egress check. This client does **not**
re-implement that SSE transport. A server that only speaks legacy SSE
stays on the codemode client. The JSON-RPC wire shape
(`initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list` →
`tools/call`, `isError` as data, transport failures as exceptions) is
the same one the codemode client proved against the live proxy.

## Transports

| Transport | How it works | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| stdio | Spawns the declared command (`shell=False`, exact argv), newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, reader thread + id correlation, stderr drained into a bounded ring | A timeout poisons the connection: all pending requests fail and the transport is torn down, so a late response can never match a recycled id. Concurrent calls are correlated by id (proven by the out-of-order test). |
| streamable HTTP | POST JSON-RPC, `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`; response parsed as plain JSON or as an SSE stream (multi-line `data:` joined per event) | `Mcp-Session-Id` is echoed when the server returns one; a 404 with a live session re-initializes once and retries once. A 202 with an empty body is an error — this client holds no GET SSE stream, so a deferred response has nowhere to arrive. |

Protocol versions: requests `2025-03-26`, accepts `2024-11-05` too,
records the negotiated version, rejects anything else. `tools/list`
follows `nextCursor` pagination. A server→client request (a message
with a `method`, even one whose id collides with a pending client id)
is answered as a request: `ping` gets an empty result, anything else
gets `-32601`. A JSON-RPC error object raises `McpError`; a tool
`isError: true` result is data (`ok: false`), not an exception.

## Declaring / enabling a server

Servers live in a JSON config (`servers.example.json` in this directory
is the example). **Servers are DISABLED BY DEFAULT** — a server runs
only when the user explicitly enables it.

```json
{"servers": [{
  "name": "echo",
  "enabled": false,
  "transport": "stdio",
  "command": ["python3", "mock_mcp_server.py",
              "/tmp/mcp-echo-marker.txt", "/tmp/mcp-echo-log.txt", "normal"],
  "env": {},
  "allowed_tools": ["echo", "read"],
  "timeout_s": 15.0
}]}
```

```python
from mcp_client import McpRegistry
reg = McpRegistry.from_dict(json.load(open("servers.example.json")))
reg.enable("echo")          # explicit: nothing runs before this
reg.connect("echo")         # spawns / dials; raises McpDisabled if disabled
reg.call("mcp.echo.echo", {"text": "hello"})
reg.list_tools()            # ['mcp.echo.echo', 'mcp.echo.read']
reg.close_all()
```

An HTTP server declaration instead:

```json
{"name": "web", "enabled": false, "transport": "http",
 "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp",
 "allowed_hosts": ["127.0.0.1"],
 "allowed_tools": ["echo"], "timeout_s": 15.0}
```

Rules enforced at config load (a bad declaration fails before any
process is spawned): name must match `[a-z0-9_-]+` and may not be
`mcp`; transport is `stdio` or `http`; duplicate server names are
rejected; unknown keys

gets `-32601`. A JSON-RPC error object raises `McpError`; a tool
`isError: true` result is data (`ok: false`), not an exception.

is the example). **Servers are DISABLED BY DEFAULT** — a server runs
only when the user explicitly enables it.

  "name": "echo",
  "enabled": false,
  "transport": "stdio",
  "command": ["python3", "mock_mcp_server.py",

  "env": {},
  "allowed_tools": ["echo", "read"],
  "timeout_s": 15.0

from mcp_client import McpRegistry

reg.connect("echo")         # spawns / dials; raises McpDisabled if disabled

An HTTP server declaration instead:

```json
{"name": "web", "enabled": false, "transport": "http",
 "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp",
 "allowed_hosts": ["127.0.0.1"],
 "allowed_tools": ["echo"], "timeout_s": 15.0}

Rules enforced at config load (a bad declaration fails before any

# Checkpoints + rollback — per-run workspace snapshot (gap #7)

Gap #7 from the 2026-11-18 agent research (§2 gap 3, §6 recommendation 7;
Cline, Claude Code, OpenCode): before the first mutation in a run,
snapshot the workspace, tag it with the run ID, expose a restore
command. This is the recovery half of the approval system — one bad
`rm` or one bad write is unrecoverable without it.

## What already existed (verified, not assumed)

The research said QwenPaw "HAS shadow-git checkpoints for workspace
files". Verified against this repo (2026-11-18):

- **No shadow-git implementation exists in this repo.** A search of
  `features/` (Python, Markdown, JS) finds the word `shadow` only as
  `shadow.git` in one place: `features/reset/reset_guard.py`
  (`PROTECTED_NAMES = {".git", "shadow.git", "media"}`) — i.e. the
  reset tool *protects* a `shadow.git` directory if one exists. That
  is a name in an allowlist, not an implementation: no code here
  creates, reads, or restores from `shadow.git`, and no checkpoint
  tool exists anywhere in the repo.
- `shadow.git` is therefore **upstream-only**: it is a directory the
  QwenPaw agent itself (v2.3.0 on the machine) maintains inside a
  workspace. Whether it actually contains per-run checkpoints on the
  live machine was **not verified** — it needs a live check on the
  machine (`ls /data/home/qwenpaw/working/workspaces/default/`), which
  this task does not do.
- What the repo *does* already know about workspace checkpoints:
  `features/infra/19-import-export.md` and `workspace-export.py`
  exclude `checkpoints/` from exports by design, and the reset tool
  deletes `W/checkpoints/` as part of the Workspaces category.

So this feature builds the missing half in the repo itself, on
tarball snapshots — it does not claim, use, or depend on shadow-git.

## Why a tarball, not a git worktree/branch

The agent workspace (`working/workspaces/default/`) is usually **not**
a git repo. A branch would need repo setup first, would silently drop
empty directories and git-ignored files, and handles large binaries
and permission bits awkwardly. A gzip tarball captures the exact bytes
(including empty directories and modes) with no repo at all, and it is
verifiable: every file is sha256-checked on restore. A DeepSeek design
review (2026-11-18, deepseek-v4.1-flash-free) agreed, and contributed
three points adopted below: full-workspace drift enumeration by
content hash (not mtime), never delete post-snapshot files without a
safety net, and 0700/0600 permissions on the store.

## Snapshot format

Default store: `<workspace>/checkpoints/` — the same name upstream
already uses, so export/reset tooling treats snapshots consistently.
`--store` overrides it (e.g. a directory outside the workspace).

```
<store>/<run-id>.tgz    gzip tarball, members sorted, mtime zeroed
<store>/<run-id>.json   manifest (see below)
```

Manifest (`<run-id>.json`, mode 0600):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `run_id`, `created_utc` | tag + UTC timestamp |
| `workspace` | absolute workspace path the snapshot was taken from |
| `files` | `{relpath: {size, sha256, mode[, link]}}` for every in-scope file |
| `file_count`, `total_bytes` | counts over the in-scope files |
| `skipped` | entries seen but NOT snapshotted, with a reason (e.g. a symlink escaping the workspace) |
| `excluded_dirs`, `excluded_file_suffixes`, `excluded_file_names` | the exclusion list that was applied |
| `tarball`, `tarball_sha256`, `tarball_bytes` | integrity of the tarball itself |

The store directory is created mode 0700; snapshot files are 0600.

**Before the FIRST mutation in a run.** The agent (or operator) runs
`snapshot` once, with the run ID, before any tool writes to the
workspace. A second snapshot with the same run ID is a **no-op that
returns the existing snapshot** — the first (pre-mutation) state
always wins. Overwriting a pre-mutation snapshot with post-mutation
state would defeat the tool, so there is no `--overw
